title.zh: 卷一百六十九 列傳第一百十九: 李訓 鄭注 王涯 王璠 賈餗 舒元輿 郭行餘 羅立言 李孝本
title.en: Volume 169 Biographies 119: Li Xun, Zheng Zhu, Wang Ya, Wang Fan, Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, Guo Xingyu, Luo Liyan, Li Xiaoben
title.raw: 卷一百六十九 列傳第一百十九: 李訓 鄭注 王涯 王璠 賈餗 舒元輿 郭行餘 羅立言 李孝本 Volume 169 Biographies 119: Li Xun, Zheng Zhu, Wang Ya, Wang Fan, Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, Guo Xingyu, Luo Liyan, Li Xiaoben

sentences.zh: 李訓，肅宗時宰相揆之族孫也。

translations.literal: Li Xun was a collateral descendant of Li Kui, who had been chancellor in the time of Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun was a collateral descendant of Li Kui, a chancellor under Emperor Suzong.

sentences.zh: 始名仲言。

translations.literal: His original name was Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 形貌魁梧，神情灑落；

translations.literal: His physique was imposing and his bearing free and easy;
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing in appearance, with an easy, unforced manner;

sentences.zh: 辭敏智捷，善揣人意。

translations.literal: his speech was quick and his wit sharp, and he was skilled at reading others' intentions.
translations.idiomatic: quick of speech and sharp of mind, and adept at divining what others were thinking.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，從父逢吉為宰相，以訓陰險善計事，愈親厚之。

translations.literal: During the Baoli reign, his cousin Li Fengji served as chancellor; because Xun was devious and adept at scheming, Fengji grew ever closer and fonder of him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli era, his cousin Li Fengji was chancellor. Fengji found Xun devious but skilled at intrigue, and drew ever closer to him.

sentences.zh: 初與茅匯等欲中傷李程，及武昭事發，訓坐長流嶺表，會赦得還。

translations.literal: At first he joined Mao Hui and others in plotting to ruin Li Cheng; when the Wuzhao affair broke out, Xun was sentenced to distant exile in Lingnan, but was able to return when an amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: He had first joined Mao Hui and others in a plot to destroy Li Cheng. When the Wuzhao affair erupted, Xun was sentenced to long exile in Lingnan, but returned when a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，居洛中。

translations.literal: After his mother's death he was in mourning and resided in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he went into mourning and lived in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時逢吉為留守，思復為宰相，且深怨裴度，居常憤郁不樂。

translations.literal: At that time Fengji was military commissioner there; he wished to become chancellor again and deeply resented Pei Du, and was constantly bitter and discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was then military commissioner at Luoyang. He longed to return to the chancellorship and bore a deep grudge against Pei Du, and was habitually bitter and ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 訓揣知其意，即以奇計動之。

translations.literal: Xun divined his intentions and stirred him with an extraordinary scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Xun read his mind and roused him with an extraordinary stratagem.

sentences.zh: 自言與鄭註善，逢吉以為然，遺訓金帛珍寶數百萬，令持入長安，以賂註。

translations.literal: He claimed to be on good terms with Zheng Zhu; Fengji believed him and gave Xun millions in gold, silk, and precious objects, ordering him to take them into Chang'an to bribe Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He said he was close to Zheng Zhu. Fengji believed him and sent Xun millions in gold, silk, and jewels to carry into Chang'an and bribe Zhu.

sentences.zh: 註得賂甚悅，乘間薦於中尉王守澄，乃以註之藥術，訓之《易》道，合薦於文宗。

translations.literal: Zhu was greatly pleased to receive the bribe; seizing an opportunity he recommended them to the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng, and on the strength of Zhu's medical arts and Xun's knowledge of the Changes, they were jointly recommended to Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was delighted with the gift. He seized a chance to recommend them to the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng, citing Zhu's medical skill and Xun's mastery of the Book of Changes, and together they were presented to Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 守澄以訓缞粗，難入禁中。

translations.literal: Shoucheng considered Xun's mourning garb too coarse for entry into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng felt that Xun's mourning dress was too rough for admission to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝令訓戎服，號王山人，與註入內。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xun to wear military dress, styled him Master Wang the Recluse, and had him enter the palace with Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Xun put on military dress, gave him the sobriquet Master Wang the Recluse, and admitted him to the palace with Zhu.

sentences.zh: 帝見其指趣，甚奇之。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw the bent of his thought, he was greatly struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by the direction of his mind and found him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 及訓釋服，在京師。

translations.literal: When Xun ended his mourning, he was in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun left mourning, he remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 太和八年，自流人補四門助教，召入內殿，面賜緋魚。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe, he was appointed from exile status as assistant instructor at the Four Gates Academy, summoned into the inner hall, and personally granted scarlet robes and the fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taihe (834), he was restored from exile to serve as assistant instructor at the Four Gates Academy, summoned to the inner hall, and personally given scarlet robes and the fish tally of office.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，遷國子《周易》博士，充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was transferred to be Doctor of the Book of Changes at the Directorate of Education and appointed Hanlin attendant lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: That October he was made Doctor of the Book of Changes at the Imperial University and Hanlin attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 入院日，賜宴，宣法曲弟子二十人就院奏法曲以寵之。

translations.literal: On the day he entered the Hanlin Academy, a banquet was given; twenty disciples of the court music office were sent to the academy to perform court music in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he entered the Hanlin, the emperor gave a banquet and sent twenty performers of court music to the academy to play in his honor.

sentences.zh: 兩省諫官伏閣切諫，言訓奸邪，海內聞知，不宜令侍宸扆，終不聽。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials of both provincial offices knelt at the gate and remonstrated urgently, saying Xun was treacherous and wicked, known throughout the realm, and unfit to attend the imperial presence; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censors from both provincial offices knelt at the gate and protested urgently that Xun was treacherous and infamous throughout the empire, and unfit to attend the throne. The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 文宗性守正嫉惡，以宦者權寵太過，繼為禍胎，元和末弒逆之徒尚在左右，雖外示優假，心不堪之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong by nature upheld rectitude and hated evil; he considered the eunuchs' power and favor excessive, a seedbed of future calamity—the regicides of late Yuanhe were still at his side—and though outwardly he showed them indulgence, inwardly he could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was upright by nature and hated wickedness. He believed the eunuchs had been granted too much power and favor, a source of coming disaster; the murderers of late Yuanhe still stood at his side. Though he treated them with outward indulgence, inwardly he could not endure them.

sentences.zh: 思欲芟落本根，以雪讎恥，九重深處，難與將相明言。

translations.literal: He wished to cut away their roots and roots of power to wipe away shame and avenge insult, but deep within the ninefold palace it was hard to speak plainly with chancellors and generals.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to uproot them and wash away the shame, but deep within the palace he could hardly speak openly with his chancellors and generals.

sentences.zh: 前與侍講宋申錫謀。

translations.literal: He had earlier plotted with the attendant lecturer Song Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier conspired with the attendant lecturer Song Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 謀之不臧，幾成反噬，自是巷伯尤橫。

translations.literal: The plot was ill-conceived and nearly turned back upon him; from then on the eunuchs grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: The plot miscarried and nearly recoiled upon him. From that time the eunuchs grew still more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 因鄭註得幸守澄，俾之援訓，冀黃門之不疑也。

translations.literal: Because Zheng Zhu had won favor with Shoucheng, he was made to support Xun, in the hope that the eunuch gate would not be suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zheng Zhu had won Shoucheng's favor, Zhu was set to back Xun, so that the eunuch establishment would not grow suspicious.

sentences.zh: 訓既在翰林，解《易》之際，或語及巷伯事，則再三憤激，以動上心。

translations.literal: Once Xun was in the Hanlin, when expounding the Changes he would sometimes speak of the eunuchs and grow repeatedly impassioned, stirring the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xun was in the Hanlin, whenever he lectured on the Changes he would sometimes speak of the eunuchs and grow repeatedly impassioned, moving the emperor's heart.

sentences.zh: 以其言論縱橫，謂其必能成事，遂以真誠謀於訓、註。

translations.literal: Because his discourse was bold and far-ranging, the emperor judged that he must be able to accomplish the deed, and confided his true intent to Xun and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His speech was bold and sweeping, and the emperor judged that he could surely bring the matter off. He then confided his true design to Xun and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 自是二人寵幸，言無不從；

translations.literal: From then on the two enjoyed imperial favor and nothing they said was refused;
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two were favored and their every word was obeyed;

sentences.zh: 而深秘之謀，往往流聞於外。

translations.literal: yet the deeply secret plans often leaked abroad.
translations.idiomatic: yet their most secret designs often leaked to the outside world.

sentences.zh: 上慮中人猜慮，乃疏《易》義六條，示於百辟，有能出訓之意者賞之，蓋欲知上以師友寵之。

translations.literal: The emperor feared the eunuchs' suspicions and therefore set forth six theses on the meaning of the Changes and displayed them to the hundred officials, promising reward to any who could discern Xun's intent—intending thereby to let it be known that the emperor cherished him as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the eunuchs' suspicion, the emperor published six theses on the meaning of the Changes and showed them to the court, promising a reward to whoever could divine Xun's meaning—so that all would know the emperor cherished him as teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，改兵部郎中、知制誥，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year he was made director in the Ministry of War, entrusted with drafting edicts, and appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year (835) he was made director in the Ministry of War, given charge of drafting edicts, and appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 九月，遷禮部侍郎、同平章事，仍賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was transferred to vice minister of rites and made associate chief councilor, and was also granted gold-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made vice minister of rites and associate chief councilor, and was granted the gold-purple robes of high office.

sentences.zh: 詔以平章之暇，三五日一入翰林。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that in his intervals from council business he should enter the Hanlin every three or five days.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to visit the Hanlin every few days when free from council duties.

sentences.zh: 訓既秉權衡，即謀誅內豎。

translations.literal: Once Xun held the scales of power, he at once plotted to execute the inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xun held the chancellorship, he immediately plotted to kill the palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 中官陳弘慶者，自元和末負弒逆之名，忠義之士無不扼腕。

translations.literal: The eunuch Chen Hongqing had borne the name of regicide since late Yuanhe; men of loyalty and righteousness all clenched their fists in rage at him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Hongqing had borne the stigma of regicide since late Yuanhe, and every loyal man gnashed his teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 時為襄陽監軍，乃召自漢南，至青泥驛，遣人封杖決殺。

translations.literal: He was then military overseer at Xiangyang; Xun summoned him from south of the Han, and at Qingni Post sent men to beat him to death with the sealed staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was then military overseer at Xiangyang. Xun summoned him from south of the Han and, at Qingni Post, had him beaten to death with the sealed staff.

sentences.zh: 王守澄自長慶已來知樞密，典禁軍，作威作福。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng had controlled the secretariat and commanded the palace armies since Changqing, wielding power and dispensing favors as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng had controlled the secretariat and commanded the palace armies since the Changqing era, making power and dispensing favors at will.

sentences.zh: 訓既作相，以守澄為六軍十二衛觀軍容使，罷其禁旅之權，尋賜鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Once Xun became chancellor he made Shoucheng commissioner for observing the armies of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, stripped him of command over the palace troops, and soon had him poisoned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xun was chancellor he made Shoucheng commissioner for observing the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, stripped him of the palace armies, and soon had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 訓愈承恩顧，每別殿奏對，他宰相莫不順成其言，黃門禁軍迎拜戢斂。

translations.literal: Xun received ever greater imperial favor; whenever he reported separately in a side hall, the other chancellors none failed to assent to his words, and the eunuchs and palace guards greeted him with bowing and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xun grew ever more favored. Whenever he reported separately in a side hall, the other chancellors assented to his every word, and the eunuchs and palace guards bowed before him in submission.

sentences.zh: 訓本以纖達，門庭趨附之士，率皆狂怪險異之流。

translations.literal: Xun by nature was slight and penetrating; those who flocked to his gate were mostly men of wild eccentricity and dangerous strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was slight and penetrating by nature, and those who thronged his gate were mostly wild, eccentric, and dangerous men.

sentences.zh: 時亦能取正人偉望，以鎮人心。

translations.literal: At times he could also win upright men of great reputation to steady popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: At times he also drew upright men of great standing to steady public opinion.

sentences.zh: 天下之人，有冀訓以致太平者，不獨人主惑其言。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm there were those who hoped Xun would bring great peace—not the emperor alone was swayed by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm there were those who hoped Xun would bring peace—not the emperor alone was taken in by his words.

sentences.zh: 訓雖為鄭註引用，及祿位俱大，勢不兩立；

translations.literal: Although Xun had been advanced through Zheng Zhu's recommendation, once their ranks and salaries were equally great, the two could not stand together;
translations.idiomatic: Though Xun had risen through Zheng Zhu's patronage, once both held high rank they could not coexist;

sentences.zh: 托以中外應赴之謀，出註為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: under the pretext of a plan requiring coordinated action inside and outside the court, he sent Zhu out as military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: and on the pretext of a plan requiring inside and outside the court to act in concert, he sent Zhu out as military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 俟誅內豎，即兼圖註。

translations.literal: He intended, once the inner eunuchs were executed, to take Zhu in hand as well.
translations.idiomatic: He meant, once the palace eunuchs were killed, to deal with Zhu as well.

sentences.zh: 約以其年十一月誅中官，須假兵力，乃以大理卿郭行余為邠寧節度使，戶部尚書王璠為太原節度使，京兆少尹羅立言權知大尹事，太府卿韓約為金吾街使，刑部郎中知雜李孝本權知中丞事，皆訓之親厚者。

translations.literal: They set the eleventh month of that year to kill the eunuchs and needed borrowed military force; therefore Guo Xingyu, chief justice of Dali, was made military commissioner of Binning; Wang Fan, minister of revenue, military commissioner of Taiyuan; Luo Liyan, vice prefect of Jingzhao, acting prefect; Han Yue, grand steward of the imperial treasury, street commissioner of the Gold Crow Guard; Li Xiaoben, director in the Ministry of Punishments with charge of miscellaneous matters, acting censor-in-chief—all men close and dear to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: They fixed the eleventh month of that year to kill the eunuchs and needed outside troops. Xun therefore appointed Guo Xingyu, chief justice of Dali, military commissioner of Binning; Wang Fan, minister of revenue, military commissioner of Taiyuan; Luo Liyan, vice prefect of Jingzhao, acting metropolitan prefect; Han Yue, grand steward of the imperial treasury, street commissioner of the Gold Crow Guard; and Li Xiaoben, director in the Ministry of Punishments with charge of miscellaneous business, acting censor-in-chief—all his close allies.

sentences.zh: 冀王璠、郭行余未赴鎮間，廣令召募豪俠及金吾臺府之從者，俾集其事。

translations.literal: He hoped that before Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu departed for their posts he could broadly order the recruitment of bold adventurers and followers of the Gold Crow Guard and the censorate to gather for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped that before Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu left for their posts he could widely recruit bold adventurers and followers of the Gold Crow Guard and the censorate to assemble for the deed.

sentences.zh: 是月二十一日，帝御紫宸。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of that month the emperor held court at Zichen.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of that month the emperor held court in the Hall of Purple Serenity.

sentences.zh: 班定，韓約不報平安，奏曰：「金吾左仗院石榴樹，夜來有甘露，臣已進狀訖。」

translations.literal: When the ranks were set, Han Yue, instead of reporting all secure, memorialized: "On the pomegranate tree in the left courtyard of the Gold Crow Guard, sweet dew appeared in the night; your servant has already submitted a report.
translations.idiomatic: When the ranks were set, Han Yue, instead of reporting all secure, memorialized: "On the pomegranate tree in the left courtyard of the Gold Crow Guard, sweet dew appeared in the night. I have already submitted a report.

sentences.zh: 乃蹈舞再拜。

translations.literal: He then danced and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: He then danced and bowed twice in celebration.

sentences.zh: 宰相百官相次稱賀。

translations.literal: Chancellors and officials in turn offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors and officials offered congratulations in turn.

sentences.zh: 李訓奏曰：「甘露降祥，俯在宮禁。

translations.literal: Li Xun memorialized: "Sweet dew has descended as an auspice, right within the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun memorialized: "Sweet dew has descended as an auspice within the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜親幸左仗觀之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should personally go to the left guard courtyard to view it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should go in person to the left guard courtyard to see it.

sentences.zh: 班退，上乘軟舁出紫宸門，由含元殿東階升殿，宰相侍臣分立於副階，文武兩班，列於殿前。

translations.literal: The session ended; the emperor mounted a palanquin and left through the Zichen Gate, ascended the eastern steps of Hanyuan Hall, with chancellors and attendants standing on either side of the secondary steps and the civil and military ranks arrayed before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Court was dismissed. The emperor rode a palanquin out through the Zichen Gate, ascended the eastern steps of Hanyuan Hall, with chancellors and attendants on the secondary steps and the civil and military ranks arrayed before the hall.

sentences.zh: 上令宰相兩省官先往視之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chancellors and officials of both provincial offices to go first and inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chancellors and officials of both provincial offices to go first and inspect it.

sentences.zh: 既還，曰：「臣等恐非真甘露，不敢輕言。

translations.literal: When they returned they said: "We fear it may not be true sweet dew and dare not speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned they said: "We fear it may not be true sweet dew and dare not speak lightly.

sentences.zh: 言出，四方必稱賀也。」

translations.literal: Once we speak, the four quarters will surely offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Once we speak, the whole realm will surely offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「韓約妄耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Has Han Yue spoken falsely?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Has Han Yue lied?"

sentences.zh: 乃令左右軍中尉、樞密內臣往視之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the chief eunuchs of the Left and Right Armies and the secretariat eunuchs to go and inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the chief eunuchs of the Left and Right Armies and the secretariat eunuchs to go and inspect it.

sentences.zh: 既去，訓召王璠、郭行余曰：「來受敕旨！」

translations.literal: After they had gone, Xun summoned Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu and said: "Come receive the imperial command!
translations.idiomatic: After they had gone, Xun summoned Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu and said: "Come receive the imperial command!

sentences.zh: 璠恐悚不能前，行余獨拜殿下。

translations.literal: Fan was terrified and could not advance; Xingyu alone bowed below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was terrified and could not advance. Xingyu alone bowed below the steps.

sentences.zh: 時兩鎮官健，皆執兵在丹鳳門外，訓已令召之，唯璠從兵入，邠寧兵竟不至。

translations.literal: At that time the soldiers of the two commands all held arms outside Danfeng Gate; Xun had already ordered them summoned, but only Fan's followers entered—the Binning troops never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of the two commands were armed outside Danfeng Gate. Xun had already ordered them summoned, but only Fan's followers entered; the Binning troops never came.

sentences.zh: 中尉、樞密至左仗，聞幕下有兵聲，驚恐走出。

translations.literal: The chief eunuchs and secretariat men reached the left guard courtyard, heard armed men beneath the curtain, and fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The chief eunuchs and secretariat men reached the left guard courtyard, heard armed men beneath the curtain, and fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 閽者欲扃鎖之，為中人所叱，執關而不能下。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers wished to bolt and lock the gate but were shouted down by the eunuchs; they held the bar but could not lower it.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers tried to bolt the gate but were shouted down by the eunuchs; they held the bar but could not drop it.

sentences.zh: 內官回奏，韓約氣懾汗流，不能舉首。

translations.literal: The eunuchs returned to report; Han Yue was cowed, streaming with sweat, and could not raise his head.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs returned to report. Han Yue was trembling and streaming with sweat and could not raise his head.

sentences.zh: 中官謂之曰：「將軍何及此耶？」

translations.literal: A eunuch said to him: "General, how could you come to this?
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch said to him: "General, how could you come to this?

sentences.zh: 又奏曰：「事急矣，請陛下入內。」

translations.literal: They also reported: "The matter is urgent; we beg Your Majesty to enter the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: They also reported: "The matter is urgent. We beg Your Majesty to enter the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 即舉軟輿迎帝。

translations.literal: They at once raised the palanquin to receive the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They at once raised the palanquin to receive the emperor.

sentences.zh: 訓殿上呼曰：「金吾衛士上殿來，護乘輿者，人賞百千。」

translations.literal: Xun shouted from the hall: "Gold Crow guards, come up to the hall! Whoever protects the palanquin shall receive a hundred thousand in reward.
translations.idiomatic: Xun shouted from the hall: "Gold Crow guards, come up to the hall! Whoever protects the palanquin shall receive a hundred thousand in reward.

sentences.zh: 內官決殿後罘罳，舉輿疾趨。

translations.literal: The eunuchs cut through the rear screen of the hall, raised the palanquin, and hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs cut through the rear screen of the hall, raised the palanquin, and hurried away.

sentences.zh: 訓攀呼曰：「陛下不得入內。」

translations.literal: Xun clung and shouted: "Your Majesty must not enter the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xun clung to the palanquin and shouted: "Your Majesty must not enter the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 金吾衛士數十人，隨訓而入。

translations.literal: Several dozen Gold Crow guards followed Xun inside.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen Gold Crow guards followed Xun inside.

sentences.zh: 羅立言率府中從人自東來，李孝本率臺中從人自西來，共四百余人，上殿縱擊內官，死傷者數十人。

translations.literal: Luo Liyan led his followers from the prefectural office from the east, Li Xiaoben led his followers from the censorate from the west—more than four hundred in all—mounted the hall and struck at the eunuchs at will; several dozen were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Liyan led more than four hundred followers from the prefectural office from the east, and Li Xiaoben led followers from the censorate from the west. They mounted the hall and struck at the eunuchs; several dozen were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 訓時愈急，邐迤入宣政門。

translations.literal: Xun grew ever more frantic and wound his way into the Xuanzheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xun grew ever more frantic and wound his way into the Xuanzheng Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝瞋目叱訓，內官郤誌榮奮拳擊其胸，訓即僵仆於地。

translations.literal: The emperor glared and rebuked Xun; the eunuch Chi Zhirong struck his chest with a fist, and Xun at once collapsed rigid to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor glared and rebuked him. The eunuch Chi Zhirong struck his chest, and Xun collapsed to the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝入東上閣門，門即闔，內官呼萬歲者數四。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the eastern upper palace gate; the gate closed at once, and the eunuchs shouted "Long live the emperor!" four times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the eastern upper palace gate. The gate closed at once, and the eunuchs shouted "Long live the emperor!" four times.

sentences.zh: 須臾，內官率禁兵五百人，露刃出閣門，遇人即殺。

translations.literal: Before long the eunuchs led five hundred palace troops with bared blades out through the gate and killed whomever they met.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the eunuchs led five hundred palace troops with bared blades out through the gate and killed whomever they met.

sentences.zh: 宰相王涯、賈餗、舒元輿、方中書會食，聞難出走，諸司從吏死者六七百人。

translations.literal: The chancellors Wang Ya, Jia Su, and Shu Yuanyu were at the Secretariat taking a meal when they heard of the crisis and fled; attendants of the various offices who died numbered six or seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors Wang Ya, Jia Su, and Shu Yuanyu were dining at the Secretariat when they heard of the crisis and fled. Attendants of the various offices who died numbered six or seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 是日，訓中拳而仆，知事不濟，乃單騎走入終南山，投寺僧宗密。

translations.literal: That day, after Xun was struck in the chest and fell, knowing the affair had failed, he rode alone into the Zhongnan Mountains and sought out the monk Zongmi.
translations.idiomatic: That day, after Xun was struck down, knowing the plot had failed, he rode alone into the Zhongnan Mountains and sought out the monk Zongmi.

sentences.zh: 訓與宗密素善，欲剃其發匿之。

translations.literal: Xun had long been on good terms with Zongmi and wished to shave his head and hide him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had long been friendly with Zongmi and wished to shave his head and hide him.

sentences.zh: 從者止之，乃趨鳳翔，欲依鄭註。

translations.literal: His followers stopped him, and he then hurried to Fengxiang intending to rely on Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His followers stopped him, and he hurried to Fengxiang intending to rely on Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 出山，為盩厔鎮將宗楚所得，械送京師。

translations.literal: When he came out of the mountains he was seized by Zong Chu, garrison commander of Zhouzhi, and sent to the capital in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: When he came out of the mountains he was seized by Zong Chu, garrison commander of Zhouzhi, and sent to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 至昆明池，訓恐入軍別受搒掠，乃謂兵士曰：「所在有兵，得我者即富貴，不如持我首行，免被奪取。」

translations.literal: At Kunming Pool, Xun feared that once he entered the army camp he would suffer beating and plunder elsewhere, and said to the soldiers: "Wherever there are troops, whoever gets me will be rich and honored; you had better carry my head and go, lest it be taken from you.
translations.idiomatic: At Kunming Pool, Xun feared that in the army camp he would be beaten and robbed by others, and said to the soldiers: "Wherever there are troops, whoever captures me will grow rich. You had better carry my head, lest another take me from you.

sentences.zh: 乃斬訓，持首而行。

translations.literal: They then beheaded Xun and went carrying his head.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded Xun and went carrying his head.

sentences.zh: 訓弟仲景、再從弟戶部員外郎元臯，皆伏法。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Zhongjian and his second cousin Yuan Gao, an outside director in the Ministry of Revenue, were both executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Zhongjian and his second cousin Yuan Gao, an outside director in the Ministry of Revenue, were both executed.

sentences.zh: 仇士良以宗密容李訓，遺人縛入左軍，責以不告之罪。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang, because Zongmi had sheltered Li Xun, sent men to bind him and bring him into the Left Army, charging him with the crime of failing to report.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang, because Zongmi had sheltered Li Xun, sent men to bind him and bring him into the Left Army, charging him with failing to report the crime.

sentences.zh: 將殺之，宗密怡然曰：「貧僧識訓年深，亦知反叛。

translations.literal: When they were about to kill him, Zongmi said calmly: "This poor monk has known Xun for many years and knew he was in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to kill him, Zongmi said calmly: "This poor monk has known Xun for many years and knew he was rebelling.

sentences.zh: 然本師教法，遇苦即救，不愛身命，死固甘心。」

translations.literal: Yet by my master's teaching, when one meets suffering one must rescue; I do not cherish life, and to die I am wholly willing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by my master's teaching, when one meets suffering one must rescue. I do not cherish my life, and I am wholly willing to die.

sentences.zh: 中尉魚弘誌嘉之，奏釋其罪。

translations.literal: The chief eunuch Yu Hongzhi praised him and memorialized to release him from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The chief eunuch Yu Hongzhi praised him and memorialized to release him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 鄭注，絳州翼城人，始以藥術遊長安權豪之門。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu was a native of Yicheng in Jiangzhou; he first wandered among the great houses of Chang'an by means of medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu was from Yicheng in Jiangzhou. He first made his way among the great houses of Chang'an through medical arts.

sentences.zh: 本姓魚，冒姓鄭氏，故時號魚鄭。

translations.literal: His original surname was Yu; he usurped the surname Zheng, and so at the time he was called Yu-Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Yu, but he took the surname Zheng, and so at the time he was called Fish-Zheng.

sentences.zh: 注用事時，人目之為「水族」。

translations.literal: When Zhu held power, people regarded him as belonging to the "aquatic clan."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu held power, people called his faction the "Aquatic Clan."

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，李愬為襄陽節度使，注往依之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, Li Su was military commissioner of Xiangyang; Zhu went to attach himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe (818), Li Su was military commissioner of Xiangyang, and Zhu went to serve him.

sentences.zh: 愬得其藥力，因厚遇之，署為節度衙推。

translations.literal: Su gained strength from his medicines and therefore treated him generously, appointing him military staff assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Su benefited from his medicines and treated him generously, appointing him military staff assessor.

sentences.zh: 從愬移鎮徐州，又為職事，軍政可否，醖與之參決。

translations.literal: When he followed Su in transfer to Xuzhou he again held office; on military and civil matters, whether yea or nay, he was always consulted in the decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Su was transferred to Xuzhou, Zhu went with him and again held office. On military and civil matters he was always consulted in the decision.

sentences.zh: 注詭辯陰狡，善探人意旨，與愬籌謀，未嘗不中其意。

translations.literal: Zhu was sophistical and secretly cunning, skilled at probing others' intentions; in planning with Su he never failed to hit his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was sophistical and secretly cunning, skilled at reading others' intentions. In planning with Su he never failed to suit his mind.

sentences.zh: 然挾邪任數，專作威福，軍府患之。

translations.literal: Yet he relied on wicked stratagems, monopolized power and favors, and the military headquarters resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he relied on wicked stratagems and monopolized power and favors, and the military headquarters resented him.

sentences.zh: 時王守澄監徐軍，深怒注。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shoucheng oversaw the Xuzhou army and deeply hated Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shoucheng oversaw the Xuzhou army and deeply hated Zhu.

sentences.zh: 一日，以軍情患注白於愬。

translations.literal: One day he reported to Su on military sentiment, saying Zhu was a source of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: One day he reported to Su that the army was troubled by Zhu.

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「彼雖如此，實奇才也。

translations.literal: Su said: "Though he is like this, he is truly a rare talent.
translations.idiomatic: Su said: "Though he is like this, he is truly a rare talent.

sentences.zh: 將軍試與之語；

translations.literal: General, try speaking with him;
translations.idiomatic: General, try speaking with him;

sentences.zh: 茍不如旨，去未為晚」愬即令謁監軍。

translations.literal: if he does not suit your mind, dismissing him will not be too late." Su at once ordered him to call on the military overseer.
translations.idiomatic: if he does not suit your mind, sending him away will not be too late." Su at once ordered him to call on the military overseer.

sentences.zh: 守澄初有難色，及延坐與語，機辯縱衡，盡中其意，遂延於內室，促膝投分，恨相見之晚。

translations.literal: Shoucheng at first looked displeased, but when he seated him and spoke with him, Zhu's wit ranged freely and wholly hit his meaning; he then brought him into an inner room, sat knee to knee, and swore friendship, regretting they had met so late.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng at first looked displeased, but when he seated Zhu and spoke with him, Zhu's wit ranged freely and wholly won him over. He brought Zhu into an inner room, sat knee to knee, and swore friendship, regretting they had met so late.

sentences.zh: 翌日，守澄謂愬曰：「誠如公言，實奇士也。」

translations.literal: The next day Shoucheng said to Su: "It is truly as you said—he is a rare talent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shoucheng said to Su: "It is truly as you said—he is a rare talent.

sentences.zh: 自是出入守澄之門，都無限隔。

translations.literal: From then on he came and went at Shoucheng's gate without any restriction.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he came and went at Shoucheng's gate without restriction.

sentences.zh: 愬署為巡官，齒於賓席。

translations.literal: Su appointed him touring officer and gave him a place among the guests.
translations.idiomatic: Su appointed him touring officer and gave him a place among the guests.

sentences.zh: 及守澄入知樞密，當長慶、寶歷之際，國政多專於守澄。

translations.literal: When Shoucheng entered to control the secretariat, during the Changqing and Baoli reigns state affairs were largely monopolized by Shoucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Shoucheng took charge of the secretariat, during the Changqing and Baoli reigns state affairs were largely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 注晝伏夜動，交通賂遺。

translations.literal: Zhu lay low by day and stirred by night, trafficking in bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu lay low by day and stirred by night, trafficking in bribes and gifts.

sentences.zh: 初則讒邪奸巧之徒附之以圖進取；

translations.literal: At first slanderous, wicked, and crafty men attached themselves to him to seek advancement;
translations.idiomatic: At first slanderous, wicked, and crafty men attached themselves to him to seek advancement;

sentences.zh: 數年之後，達僚權臣，爭湊其門。

translations.literal: after several years, high officials and powerful ministers all crowded his gate.
translations.idiomatic: after several years, high officials and powerful ministers all crowded his gate.

sentences.zh: 累從山東、京西諸軍，歷衛佐、評事、御史，又檢校庫部郎中，為昭義節度副使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed armies in Shandong and west of the capital, serving as guard aide, reviewer, and censor, and was also acting director in the Ministry of Treasury, and deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly followed armies in Shandong and west of the capital, serving as guard aide, reviewer, and censor, and was also acting director in the Ministry of Treasury and deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 既以陰事誣陷宋申錫，守道正人，始側目焉。

translations.literal: Once he had framed Song Shenxi on a secret charge, upright men who upheld the Way began to look askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had framed Song Shenxi on a secret charge, upright men who upheld the Way began to look askance at him.

sentences.zh: 太和七年，罷邠寧行軍司馬，入京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe he was dismissed as marching commander of Binning and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe (833) he was dismissed as marching commander of Binning and entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 御史李款閣內彈之曰：「鄭注內通敕使，外結朝官，兩地往來，卜射財貨，晝伏夜動，幹竊化權。

translations.literal: The censor Li Kuan impeached him within the gate, saying: "Zheng Zhu communicates inward with edict-bearers and outward binds court officials; between the two realms he goes back and forth, divining and seizing wealth, lying low by day and stirring by night, usurping transforming power.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Li Kuan impeached him within the gate, saying: "Zheng Zhu communicates inward with edict-bearers and outward binds court officials. Between the two realms he goes back and forth, seizing wealth, lying low by day and stirring by night, usurping transforming power.

sentences.zh: 人不敢言，道路以目。

translations.literal: People dare not speak; on the road they signal with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: People dare not speak; on the road they signal with their eyes alone.

sentences.zh: 請付法司。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be handed to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be handed to the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 旬日內，諫章十數，文宗不納。

translations.literal: Within ten days more than a dozen remonstrance memorials arrived; Emperor Wenzong would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days more than a dozen remonstrance memorials arrived; Emperor Wenzong would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 尋授注通王府司馬，充右神策判官，中外駭嘆。

translations.literal: Soon Zhu was appointed prince of Tong's staff marshal and served as judge of the Right Divine Strategy Army; court and countryside were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu was appointed staff marshal to the Prince of Tong and judge of the Right Divine Strategy Army; court and countryside were appalled.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，注進藥方一卷，令守澄召注對浴堂門，賜錦彩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year Zhu presented a volume of medical formulas; Shoucheng was ordered to summon Zhu for audience at the Bath Hall gate and grant him brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year (834) Zhu presented a volume of medical formulas. Shoucheng was ordered to summon Zhu for audience at the Bath Hall gate and grant him brocade.

sentences.zh: 召對之夕，彗出東方，長三尺，光耀甚緊。

translations.literal: On the night of the audience a comet appeared in the east, three feet long, its light very intense.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the audience a comet appeared in the east, three feet long, its light very intense.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，拜太僕卿、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he was appointed grand master of stud and concurrent censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year he was appointed grand master of stud and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 注起第善和裏，通於永巷，長廊復壁。

translations.literal: Zhu built a mansion in Shanhe Lane, connected to the Eternal Lane, with long corridors and double walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu built a mansion in Shanhe Lane, connected to the Eternal Lane, with long corridors and double walls.

sentences.zh: 日聚京師輕薄子弟、方鎮將吏，以招權利。

translations.literal: Daily he gathered frivolous young men of the capital and generals and officials of the provinces to draw power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he gathered frivolous young men of the capital and generals and officials of the provinces to draw power and profit.

sentences.zh: 間日入禁軍，與守澄款密，語必移時，或通夕不寐。

translations.literal: Every few days he entered the palace armies and spoke intimately with Shoucheng; their talk always lasted a long while, sometimes the whole night without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Every few days he entered the palace armies and spoke intimately with Shoucheng. Their talk always lasted a long while, sometimes the whole night without sleep.

sentences.zh: 李訓既附注以進，承間入謁；

translations.literal: Li Xun, having attached himself to Zhu to advance, seized opportunities to call on him;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, having attached himself to Zhu to advance, seized opportunities to call on him;

sentences.zh: 而輕浮躁進者，盈於注門。

translations.literal: and frivolous, rash climbers filled Zhu's gate.
translations.idiomatic: and frivolous, rash climbers filled Zhu's gate.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，遷工部尚書，充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year he was transferred to minister of works and appointed Hanlin attendant lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year (835) he was transferred to minister of works and appointed Hanlin attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 召自九仙門，帝面賜告身。

translations.literal: He was summoned from the Nine Immortals Gate and the emperor personally granted him his commission of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned from the Nine Immortals Gate and the emperor personally granted him his commission of office.

sentences.zh: 時李訓已在禁庭，二人相洽，日侍君側，講貫太平之術，以為朝夕可致升平。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xun was already in the inner court; the two were in harmony, daily attending the ruler's side, lecturing on the arts of great peace, believing that order could be brought in a morning and an evening.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xun was already in the inner court. The two were in harmony, daily attending the ruler's side, lecturing on the arts of great peace, believing that order could be brought in a morning and an evening.

sentences.zh: 兩奸合從，天子益惑其說。

translations.literal: The two villains joined forces, and the Son of Heaven was ever more beguiled by their words.
translations.idiomatic: The two villains joined forces, and the Son of Heaven was ever more beguiled by their words.

sentences.zh: 是時，訓、注之權，赫於天下。

translations.literal: At that time the power of Xun and Zhu blazed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the power of Xun and Zhu blazed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 既得行其志，生平恩仇，絲毫必報。

translations.literal: Once they could carry out their will, every favor and grudge of their lives was repaid to the last thread.
translations.idiomatic: Once they could carry out their will, every favor and grudge of their lives was repaid to the last thread.

sentences.zh: 因楊虞卿之獄，挾忌李宗閔、李德裕，心所惡者，目為二人之黨。

translations.literal: Using the case of Yang Yuqing, they bore malice toward Li Zongmin and Li Deyu; whoever they hated in heart they labeled a partisan of the two.
translations.idiomatic: Using the case of Yang Yuqing, they bore malice toward Li Zongmin and Li Deyu. Whoever they hated they labeled a partisan of the two.

sentences.zh: 朝士相繼斥逐，班列為之一空，人人惴栗，若崩厥角。

translations.literal: Court officials were driven out one after another; the ranks were emptied, and every man trembled in fear as if his horns would break.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were driven out one after another. The ranks were emptied, and every man trembled in fear as if the sky were falling.

sentences.zh: 帝微知之，下詔慰諭，人情稍安。

translations.literal: The emperor slightly understood this and issued an edict of comfort and instruction; popular feeling grew somewhat calmer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor slightly understood this and issued an edict of comfort and instruction. Popular feeling grew somewhat calmer.

sentences.zh: 訓、注天資狂妄，偷合茍容，至於經略謀猷，無可稱者。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu were arrogant by nature, clinging together in unprincipled accommodation; as for grand strategy and counsel, there was nothing to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu were arrogant by nature and clung together in unprincipled accommodation. As for grand strategy and counsel, there was nothing to praise.

sentences.zh: 初浴堂召對，上訪以富人之術，乃以榷茶為對。

translations.literal: At the first Bath Hall audience the emperor inquired about methods to enrich the state, and he answered with a monopoly on tea.
translations.idiomatic: At the first Bath Hall audience the emperor inquired about methods to enrich the state, and Zhu answered with a monopoly on tea.

sentences.zh: 其法，欲以江湖百姓茶園，官自造作，量給直分，命使者主之。

translations.literal: The method was to have the government itself manufacture tea from the tea gardens of common people along the rivers and lakes, measure out payment in shares, and appoint envoys to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: The method was to have the government itself manufacture tea from the tea gardens of common people along the rivers and lakes, measure out payment in shares, and appoint envoys to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 帝惑其言，乃命王涯兼榷茶使。

translations.literal: The emperor was swayed by his words and ordered Wang Ya to serve concurrently as tea monopoly commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was swayed by his words and ordered Wang Ya to serve concurrently as tea monopoly commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又言秦中有災，宜興工役以禳之。

translations.literal: He also said that Qin had suffered disaster and that public works should be launched to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Qin had suffered disaster and that public works should be launched to avert it.

sentences.zh: 文宗能詩，嘗吟杜甫《江頭篇》云：「江頭宮殿鎖千門，細柳新蒲為誰綠？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong could compose poetry and once recited Du Fu's "By the River" saying: "Palaces by the river lock a thousand gates—for whom do the slender willows and fresh reeds grow green?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong could compose poetry and once recited Du Fu's "By the River": "Palaces by the river lock a thousand gates—for whom do the slender willows and fresh reeds grow green?

sentences.zh: 始知天寶已前，環曲江四岸，有樓臺行宮廨署，心切慕之。

translations.literal: He then learned that before Tianbao, all around the four banks of Qujiang there had been terraces, traveling palaces, and offices, and he deeply yearned for this.
translations.idiomatic: He then learned that before Tianbao, all around the four banks of Qujiang there had been terraces, traveling palaces, and offices, and he deeply yearned for this.

sentences.zh: 既得注言，即命左右神策軍差人淘曲江、昆明二池，仍許公卿士大夫之家於江頭立亭館，以時追賞。

translations.literal: Once he had Zhu's word, he at once ordered the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies to send men to dredge Qujiang and Kunming pools, and also allowed the households of dukes, ministers, and literati to build pavilions and lodges by the river for seasonal enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had Zhu's word, he at once ordered the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies to dredge Qujiang and Kunming pools, and also allowed the households of dukes, ministers, and literati to build pavilions and lodges by the river for seasonal enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 時兩軍造紫雲樓、彩霞亭，內出樓額以賜之。

translations.literal: At that time the two armies built the Purple Cloud Tower and the Colored Mist Pavilion; the inner court issued the building plaques as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the two armies built the Purple Cloud Tower and the Colored Mist Pavilion. The inner court issued the building plaques as gifts.

sentences.zh: 注言無不從，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Nothing Zhu said was refused—all were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing Zhu said was refused—all were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 九月，檢校尚書左僕射、鳳翔尹、鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, prefect of Fengxiang, and military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, prefect of Fengxiang, and military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 蓋與李訓謀事有期，欲中外協勢。

translations.literal: This was because he and Li Xun had fixed a date for their plot and wished inside and outside the court to coordinate their strength.
translations.idiomatic: This was because he and Li Xun had fixed a date for their plot and wished inside and outside the court to coordinate their strength.

sentences.zh: 十一月，註聞訓事發，自鳳翔率親兵五百餘人赴闕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhu heard that Xun's affair had broken out and led more than five hundred personal troops from Fengxiang to hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhu heard that Xun's plot had broken out and led more than five hundred personal troops from Fengxiang to hurry to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至扶風，聞訓敗，乃還。

translations.literal: When he reached Fufeng he heard Xun had been defeated and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Fufeng he heard Xun had been defeated and turned back.

sentences.zh: 監軍使張仲清已得密詔，迎而勞之，召至監軍府議事。

translations.literal: The military overseer Zhang Zhongqing had already received a secret edict; he went out to welcome and console him and summoned him to the overseer's headquarters to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The military overseer Zhang Zhongqing had already received a secret edict. He went out to welcome and console Zhu and summoned him to the overseer's headquarters to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 注倚兵衛即赴之，仲清已伏兵幕下。

translations.literal: Zhu, relying on his armed escort, went at once; Zhongqing had already hidden troops beneath the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, relying on his armed escort, went at once. Zhongqing had already hidden troops beneath the curtain.

sentences.zh: 注方坐，伏兵發，斬注，傳首京師，部下潰散。

translations.literal: As Zhu had just seated himself the hidden troops sprang forth, beheaded Zhu, and sent his head to the capital; his followers scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhu had just seated himself the hidden troops sprang forth, beheaded Zhu, and sent his head to the capital. His followers scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 注家屬屠滅，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: Zhu's family was slaughtered to the last; not one survived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's family was slaughtered to the last. Not one survived.

sentences.zh: 初未獲注，京師憂恐。

translations.literal: At first, before Zhu was captured, the capital was anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before Zhu was captured, the capital was anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 至是，人人相慶。

translations.literal: When this happened, everyone congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When this happened, everyone congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 注兩目不能遠視，自言有金丹之術，可去痿弱重膇之疾。

translations.literal: Zhu's two eyes could not see far; he claimed to possess the art of the golden elixir, which could remove the ailments of weakness and heavy legs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's two eyes could not see far. He claimed to possess the art of the golden elixir, which could remove the ailments of weakness and heavy legs.

sentences.zh: 始李愬自云得效，乃移之守澄，亦神其事。

translations.literal: At first Li Su said he had obtained effect, then the claim was transferred to Shoucheng, who also regarded the matter as miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Su said he had obtained effect, then the claim was transferred to Shoucheng, who also regarded the matter as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 由是中官視注皆憐之，卒以是售其狂謀。

translations.literal: Because of this the eunuchs all looked on Zhu with pity, and in the end he sold his mad plot through this means.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the eunuchs all looked on Zhu with pity, and in the end he sold his mad plot through this means.

sentences.zh: 而守澄自貽其患，復致衣冠塗地，豈一時之沴氣歟？

translations.literal: Yet Shoucheng brought disaster on himself and again brought the gentry to ruin—was it only the baleful qi of a single moment?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shoucheng brought disaster on himself and again brought the gentry to ruin—was it only the baleful air of a single moment?

sentences.zh: 既籍沒其家財，得絹一百萬匹，他貨稱是。

translations.literal: Once his household property was confiscated, there were found a million bolts of silk and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Once his household property was confiscated, there were found a million bolts of silk and other goods in proportion.

sentences.zh: 王涯，字廣津，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Ya, style name Guangjin, was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, style name Guangjin, was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父晃。

translations.literal: His father was Huang.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Huang.

sentences.zh: 涯，貞元八年進士擢第，登宏辭科。

translations.literal: Ya passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Zhenyuan and also passed the macro-elocution examination.
translations.idiomatic: Ya passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Zhenyuan (792) and also passed the macro-elocution examination.

sentences.zh: 釋褐藍田尉。

translations.literal: On leaving the russet he served as aide of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the russet he served as aide of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十年十一月，召充翰林學士，拜右拾遺、左補闕、起居舍人，皆充內職。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year of Zhenyuan he was summoned as Hanlin academician and appointed right remonstrance official, left supplementer, and recorder of conduct—all inner-service posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year of Zhenyuan (804) he was summoned as Hanlin academician and appointed right remonstrance official, left supplementer, and recorder of conduct—all inner-service posts.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，為宰相李吉甫所怒，罷學士，守都官員外郎，再貶虢州司馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe he incurred the anger of Chancellor Li Jifu, was removed as academician, retained as outside director of the capital magistracy, and was again demoted to military aide of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe (808) he incurred the anger of Chancellor Li Jifu, was removed as academician, retained as outside director of the capital magistracy, and was again demoted to military aide of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，入為吏部員外。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered the capital as outside director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (810) he entered the capital as outside director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 七年，改兵部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to outside director in the Ministry of War and entrusted with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (812) he was transferred to outside director in the Ministry of War and entrusted with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，正拜舍人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year he was formally appointed drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year (814) he was formally appointed drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉工部侍郎、知制誥，加通議大夫、清源縣開國男，學士如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to vice minister of works with charge of drafting edicts, promoted to gentleman for spreading governance, and made Baron of Qingyuan County, remaining academician as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (815) he was transferred to vice minister of works with charge of drafting edicts, promoted to gentleman for spreading governance, and made Baron of Qingyuan County, remaining academician as before.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，加中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year (816) he was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月，罷相，守兵部侍郎，尋遷吏部。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year he was removed as chancellor and retained as vice minister of war, soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year (818) he was removed as chancellor and retained as vice minister of war, soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Ya was made acting minister of rites, prefect of Zi, and military commissioner of Eastern Chuan in the Sword South.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Ya was made acting minister of rites, prefect of Zi, and military commissioner of Eastern Chuan in the Sword South.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，吐蕃南北倚角入寇，西北邊騷動，詔兩川兵拒之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year the Tibetans invaded from north and south in concert; the northwest frontier was disturbed, and an edict ordered the armies of the two Chuan commands to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year the Tibetans invaded from north and south in concert. The northwest frontier was disturbed, and an edict ordered the armies of the two Chuan commands to resist.

sentences.zh: 時蕃軍逼雅州，涯上疏曰：「臣當道出軍，徑入賊腹有兩路：一路從龍州清川鎮入蕃界，徑抵故松州城，是吐蕃舊置節度之所；

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetan army pressed Ya Prefecture; Ya submitted a memorial saying: "When your servant leads troops out on the proper route, there are two ways to enter the enemy's belly directly: one from Qingchuan Town in Long Prefecture into Tibetan territory, straight to the old Song Prefecture city, where the Tibetans formerly placed their military commission;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tibetan army pressed Ya Prefecture. Ya submitted a memorial saying: "When I lead troops out on the proper route, there are two ways to enter the enemy's belly directly: one from Qingchuan Town in Long Prefecture into Tibetan territory, straight to the old Song Prefecture city, where the Tibetans formerly placed their military commission;

sentences.zh: 一路從綿州威蕃柵入蕃界，徑抵棲雞城，皆吐蕃險要之地。」

translations.literal: one from the Weifan Stockade in Mian Prefecture into Tibetan territory, straight to Qiji City—all critical Tibetan strongpoints.
translations.idiomatic: one from the Weifan Stockade in Mian Prefecture into Tibetan territory, straight to Qiji City—all critical Tibetan strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣伏見方今天下無犬吠之警，海內同覆盂之安。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant observes that at present under Heaven there is no alarm of a dog's bark; within the seas all share the security of an overturned bowl.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I observe that at present under Heaven there is no alarm of a dog's bark; within the seas all share the security of an overturned bowl.

sentences.zh: 每蕃戎一警，則中外咸震，致陛下有旰食軫懷之憂，斯乃臣等居大官、受重寄者之深責也。

translations.literal: Whenever the frontier tribes sound one alarm, court and countryside alike are shaken, bringing Your Majesty the worry of eating late and caring deeply—this is the heavy responsibility of your servants who hold high office and receive great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the frontier tribes sound one alarm, court and countryside alike are shaken, bringing Your Majesty the worry of eating late and caring deeply—this is the heavy responsibility of us who hold high office and receive great trust.

sentences.zh: 雖承詔發卒，心馳寇廷，期於為國討除，使戎人芟剪。

translations.literal: Though we receive edicts to raise troops, our hearts race to the enemy court, hoping to purge them for the state and cut down the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Though we receive edicts to raise troops, our hearts race to the enemy court, hoping to purge them for the state and cut down the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 晝夜思忖，何補涓毫？

translations.literal: Day and night we ponder—what help is a mere drop?
translations.idiomatic: Day and night we ponder—what help is a mere drop?

sentences.zh: 所以淒淒愚心，願陳萬一。

translations.literal: Therefore with sorrowful foolish heart I wish to set forth one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with sorrowful foolish heart I wish to set forth one part in ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 臣觀自古長策，昭然可征。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that long-term policies since antiquity are clear and can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that long-term policies since antiquity are clear and can be verified.

sentences.zh: 在於實邊兵，選良將，明斥候，廣資儲，杜其奸謀，險其走集，此立朝士大夫皆知，不獨微臣知之也，只在舉行之耳。

translations.literal: They lie in strengthening frontier troops, selecting good generals, clarifying scouts, broadening stores, blocking their secret plots, and making dangerous their routes of flight and gathering—this every court scholar-official knows, not your servant alone; it only awaits being carried out.
translations.idiomatic: They lie in strengthening frontier troops, selecting good generals, clarifying scouts, broadening stores, blocking their secret plots, and making dangerous their routes of flight and gathering—this every court scholar-official knows, not I alone; it only awaits being carried out.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚見所及，猶欲布露者，誠願陛下不愛金帛之費，以釣北虜之心。

translations.literal: Yet what your servant's foolish view reaches and still wishes to disclose is truly to beg Your Majesty not to spare gold and silk, in order to hook the hearts of the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what my foolish view reaches and still wishes to disclose is truly to beg Your Majesty not to spare gold and silk, in order to hook the hearts of the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 臨遣信臣，與之定約曰：犬戎悖亂負恩，為邊鄙患者數矣，能制而服之者，唯在北蕃。

translations.literal: Send a trusted minister to fix a covenant with them, saying: The Rong dogs have been rebellious and ungrateful, troubling the borderlands many times; only the northern tribes can control and subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Send a trusted minister to fix a covenant with them, saying: The Rong dogs have been rebellious and ungrateful, troubling the borderlands many times; only the northern tribes can control and subdue them.

sentences.zh: 如能發兵深入，殺若干人，取若干地，則受若干之賞。

translations.literal: If they can send troops deep in, kill so many men, take so much land, they shall receive so much reward.
translations.idiomatic: If they can send troops deep in, kill so many men, take so much land, they shall receive so much reward.

sentences.zh: 開懷以示之，厚利以啗之，所以勸聳要約者異於他日，則匈奴之銳，可得出矣。

translations.literal: Open your heart to show them, use thick profit to feed them—if the encouragement and binding of the covenant differ from other days, then the Xiongnu's sharp edge can be drawn forth.
translations.idiomatic: Open your heart to show them, use thick profit to feed them—if the encouragement and binding of the covenant differ from other days, then the Xiongnu's sharp edge can be drawn forth.

sentences.zh: 一戰之後，西戎之力衰矣。」

translations.literal: After one battle the strength of the western Rong will decline.
translations.idiomatic: After one battle the strength of the western Rong will decline.

sentences.zh: 穆宗不能用其謀。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong could not use his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong could not use his plan.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，幽、鎮復亂，王師征之，未聞克捷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing You and Zhen rebelled again; the imperial armies campaigned against them, but no victory was heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing (821) You and Zhen rebelled again. The imperial armies campaigned against them, but no victory was heard.

sentences.zh: 涯在鎮上書論用兵曰：

translations.literal: Ya, in his command, submitted a memorial discussing the use of troops, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ya, in his command, submitted a memorial discussing the use of troops, saying:

sentences.zh: 伏以幽、鎮兩州，悖亂天紀，迷亭育之厚德，肆豺虎之非心。

translations.literal: I submit that the two prefectures You and Zhen have rebelled against Heaven's order, lost in thick nurturing virtue, and unleashed the wolfish hearts of jackals and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the two prefectures You and Zhen have rebelled against Heaven's order, lost in thick nurturing virtue, and unleashed the wolfish hearts of jackals and tigers.

sentences.zh: 囚系鼎臣，戕賊戎帥，毒流列郡，釁及賓僚。

translations.literal: They imprisoned great ministers, killed military commanders, poison spread through the commanderies, and trouble reached guests and aides.
translations.idiomatic: They imprisoned great ministers, killed military commanders, poison spread through the commanderies, and trouble reached guests and aides.

sentences.zh: 凡在有情，孰不扼腕？

translations.literal: All who have feeling—who does not clench his fists?
translations.idiomatic: All who have feeling—who does not clench his fists?

sentences.zh: 咸欲橫戈荷戟，問罪賊廷。

translations.literal: All wish to level spears and bear halberds, to demand justice at the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: All wish to level spears and bear halberds, to demand justice at the rebel court.

sentences.zh: 伏以國家文德誕敷，武功繼立，遠無不服，邇無不安。

translations.literal: I submit that the state's civil virtue is broadly spread and martial achievement stands in succession; far off none fail to submit, near at hand none fail to be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the state's civil virtue is broadly spread and martial achievement stands in succession. Far off none fail to submit, near at hand none fail to be at peace.

sentences.zh: 矧茲二方，敢逆天理？

translations.literal: How much more these two regions—how dare they oppose Heaven's principle?
translations.idiomatic: How much more these two regions—how dare they oppose Heaven's principle?

sentences.zh: 臣竊料詔書朝下，諸鎮夕驅，以貔貅問罪之師，當猖狂失節之寇，傾山壓卵，決海灌熒，勢之相懸，不是過也。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to judge that when the edict is issued in the morning the commands will march by evening; with tiger-and-dragon armies demanding justice against wildly unbridled rebels, overturning mountains to crush eggs, deciding seas to pour out flames—the disparity of force could hardly be greater.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to judge that when the edict is issued in the morning the commands will march by evening. With tiger-and-dragon armies demanding justice against wildly unbridled rebels, overturning mountains to crush eggs, deciding seas to pour out flames—the disparity of force could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 但以常山、燕郡，虞、虢相依，一時興師，恐費財力。

translations.literal: But because Changshan and Yan commandery, Yu and Guo, lean on one another, to raise armies at once may waste wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: But because Changshan and Yan commandery, Yu and Guo, lean on one another, to raise armies at once may waste wealth and strength.

sentences.zh: 且夫罪有輕重，事有後先，攻堅宜從易者。

translations.literal: Moreover guilt has light and heavy degrees, affairs have first and later order; in attacking the hard one should begin with the easy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover guilt has light and heavy degrees, affairs have first and later order. In attacking the hard one should begin with the easy.

sentences.zh: 如聞范陽肇亂，出自一時，事非宿謀，情亦可驗。

translations.literal: As I have heard, the rebellion at Fanyang began at a single moment; the affair was not a long-planned conspiracy, and the circumstances can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the Fanyang rebellion arose suddenly, not from a long-standing plot—a reading the facts bear out.

sentences.zh: 鎮州構禍，殊匪偶然，扇動屬城，以兵拒境。

translations.literal: Zhen Prefecture brought calamity—utterly not by chance—stirring its subordinate cities and using troops to block the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble at Zhenzhou was hardly accidental: they stirred neighboring cities and deployed troops to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如此則幽、薊之眾，可示寬刑；

translations.literal: If so, toward the masses of You and Ji one may show lenient punishment;
translations.idiomatic: On that basis, the people of You and Ji could be offered clemency;

sentences.zh: 鎮、冀之戎，必資先討。

translations.literal: the warriors of Zhen and Ji must rely on being attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: while the forces of Zhen and Ji must be dealt with first.

sentences.zh: 況廷湊亹茸，不席父祖之恩；

translations.literal: Moreover Ting Cou is weak and ineffectual, not inheriting the kindness of father and ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Tingcou is feeble and unworthy, having no claim to his forebears' legacy;

sentences.zh: 成德分離，人多迫脅之勢。

translations.literal: Chengde is divided, and most people are under the momentum of coercion.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde is fragmented, and most of its people follow under duress.

sentences.zh: 今以魏博思復讎之眾，昭義願盡敵之師，參之晉陽，輔以滄、易，掎角而進，易若建瓴，盡屠其城，然後北首燕路。

translations.literal: Now, with the Weibo masses eager to avenge a grudge, the Zhaoyi army willing to exhaust the enemy, joined with Jinyang, assisted by Cang and Yi, advancing in pincer—easy as pouring from a high eave—slaughtering their cities entirely, then turning north toward the road to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy Weibo's troops, burning for revenge, and Zhaoyi's forces, eager to crush the foe; add Jinyang and support from Cangzhou and Yizhou. Advance in pincers—swift as water poured from a high roof—level their cities, then march north toward Yan.

sentences.zh: 在朝廷不為失信，於軍勢實得機宜。

translations.literal: For the court this would not be breaking faith; for military force it truly accords with the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not appear to break faith, and militarily the timing would be exactly right.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚忠，輒在於此。

translations.literal: Your servant's foolish loyalty lies precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: My humble counsel comes down to this.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞用兵若鬥，先扼其喉。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that in using troops as in combat, one first seizes the throat.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that in war, as in a fight, one must first seize the enemy's throat.

sentences.zh: 今瀛、莫、易、定，兩賊之咽喉也，誠宜假之威柄，戍以重兵。

translations.literal: Now Ying, Mo, Yi, and Ding are the throat of the two rebels; truly one should lend them authority and garrison them with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Mo, Yi, and Ding are the two rebels' jugular. They should be granted real authority and garrisoned with strong forces.

sentences.zh: 俾其死生不相知，間諜無所入，而以大軍先迫冀、趙，次下井陘，此百舉百全之勢也。

translations.literal: So that they know nothing of each other's life or death, spies have nowhere to enter; then with the main army first pressing Ji and Zhao, next descending Jingxing Pass—this is a posture of a hundred attempts, a hundred successes.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off their communications so spies cannot penetrate; then drive the main army first against Ji and Zhao and next down Jingxing Pass—a strategy that cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩深至，無以上酬，輕冒陳聞，不勝戰越。

translations.literal: Your servant has received grace deep beyond measure and has no way to repay it above; I lightly dare to report this, unable to overcome trembling dread.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace to me runs so deep that I can never repay it; I venture this report with fear and trembling.

sentences.zh: 洎涯疏至，盧士玫已為賊劫，陷瀛、莫州，兇勢不可遏。

translations.literal: By the time Ya's memorial arrived, Lu Shimei had already been seized by rebels; Ying and Mo prefectures had fallen—the fierce momentum could not be checked.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Ya's memorial reached court, Lu Shimei had already been taken by the rebels and Ying and Mo had fallen—the rebellion's fury could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 俄而二兇俱宥之。

translations.literal: Soon both rebels were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both rebel leaders were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered the capital as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to serve as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，改戶部侍郎、兼御史大夫，充鹽鐵轉運使，俄遷禮部尚書，充職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he was changed to vice minister of revenue, concurrently censor-in-chief, and made salt and iron transport commissioner; soon he was transferred to minister of rites, continuing in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong succeeded to the throne, Ya became vice minister of revenue and concurrent censor-in-chief, and was appointed salt and iron transport commissioner; he was soon promoted to minister of rites while retaining those duties.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，檢校尚書左僕射、興元尹、山南西道節度使，就加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli he was made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, prefect of Xingyuan, and military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit; at the same time he was further made acting grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoli year 2 (826) he was appointed acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, prefect of Xingyuan, and military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, with the concurrent rank of acting grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 太和三年正月，入為太常卿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Taihe he entered the capital as grand master of court music.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taihe year 3 (829) he returned to the capital as grand master of court music.

sentences.zh: 文宗以樂府之音，鄭衛太甚，欲聞古樂，命涯詢於舊工，取開元時雅樂，選樂童按之，名曰《雲韶樂》。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, because the music of the Music Bureau was too much Zheng and Wei, wished to hear ancient music; he ordered Ya to inquire of old craftsmen, take the elegant music of the Kaiyuan era, select music boys to perform it, and name it "Yunshao Music."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong found the Music Bureau's repertoire too decadent—too much Zheng and Wei—and wished to hear ancient music. He had Ya consult veteran musicians, recover the elegant Kaiyuan-era pieces, and have young performers rehearse them under the title "Yunshao Music."

sentences.zh: 樂曲成，涯與太常丞李廓、少府監庾承憲、押樂工獻於黎園亭，帝按之於會昌殿。

translations.literal: When the music was complete, Ya with Vice Director of Court Music Li Kuo, Director of the Palace Manufactories Yu Chengxian, and supervising musicians presented it at Liyuan Pavilion; the Emperor examined it at Huichang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the piece was ready, Ya, Vice Director of Court Music Li Kuo, Director of the Palace Manufactories Yu Chengxian, and the supervising musicians presented it at Liyuan Pavilion, and the Emperor heard it performed at Huichang Hall.

sentences.zh: 上悅，賜涯等錦彩。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and bestowed brocades upon Ya and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and rewarded Ya and his colleagues with brocades.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，守吏部尚書、檢校司空，復領鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he served as minister of civil office, acting grand mentor, and again headed the salt and iron transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 4 he served as minister of civil office and acting grand mentor, and again took charge of the salt and iron transport commission.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，守左僕射，領使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he served as left vice director and continued as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That September he became left vice director while continuing as transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏李師道前據河南十二州，其兗、鄆、淄、青、濮州界，舊有銅鐵冶，每年額利百餘萬，自收復，未定稅額，請復係鹽鐵司，依建中元年九月敕例制置，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Li Shidao had formerly held twelve prefectures south of the Yellow River; within the borders of Yan, Yun, Zi, Qing, and Pu there had been copper and iron smelters yielding over a million in annual quota profit—since reconquest the tax quota had not been fixed; he requested restoring it to the salt and iron office and arranging it according to the ninth-month edict precedent of the first year of Jianzhong; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Li Shidao had once controlled twelve prefectures south of the Yellow River. The Yan, Yun, Zi, Qing, and Pu region had long had copper and iron works yielding over a million strings in annual profits; since reconquest no tax quota had been set. He asked that the industry be returned to the Salt and Iron Commission and administered under the Jianzhong 1 (780) ninth-month precedent. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，以本官同平章事，進封代國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year, with his existing office he became co-chancellor; he was advanced in rank to Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 7 he was made co-chancellor in his existing post, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，加檢校司空、門下侍郎、弘文館大學士、太清宮使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he was further made acting grand mentor, vice director of the Chancellery, grand scholar of the Hongwen Library, and commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 8 he was further appointed acting grand mentor, vice director of the Chancellery, grand scholar of the Hongwen Library, and commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace.

sentences.zh: 九年五月，正拜司空，仍令所司冊命，加開府儀同三司，仍兼領江南榷茶使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year he was formally invested as grand mentor, with the responsible offices ordered to confer the patent of appointment; he was further made honorary grand general with fiefs, and still concurrently headed the Jiangnan tea monopoly commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 9 he was formally appointed grand mentor with full investiture, given the honorary rank of grand general of the open office, and continued concurrently as Jiangnan tea monopoly commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十一日，李訓事敗，文宗入內。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, Li Xun's affair failed; Wenzong entered the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the eleventh month Li Xun's plot collapsed and Emperor Wenzong retreated to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 涯與同列歸中書會食，未下箸，吏報有兵自閣門出，逢人即殺。

translations.literal: Ya and his colleagues returned to the Secretariat to dine together; before they had taken chopsticks an aide reported that troops had come out from the Gate Pavilion and were killing whomever they met.
translations.idiomatic: Ya and his fellow officials had returned to the Secretariat for a meal when, before they could begin eating, a clerk reported that soldiers had burst from the Gate Pavilion and were killing everyone they encountered.

sentences.zh: 涯等蒼惶步出，至永昌裏茶肆，為禁兵所擒，並其家屬奴婢，皆繫於獄。

translations.literal: Ya and the others fled in panic on foot; reaching a teahouse in Yongchang Lane, they were seized by the imperial guard; together with their families and servants, all were bound in prison.
