translations.idiomatic: Ya and the others fled on foot in panic to a teahouse in Yongchang Lane, where the palace guard seized them. Their families and servants were all thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 仇士良鞫涯反狀，涯實不知其故。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang interrogated Ya on the particulars of rebellion; Ya truly did not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang interrogated Ya on charges of treason, but Ya genuinely knew nothing of the plot.

sentences.zh: 械縛既急，搒笞不勝其酷，乃令手書反狀，自誣與訓同謀。

translations.literal: Once shackling was tightened and flogging could not bear the cruelty, he was made to write by hand the particulars of rebellion, falsely implicating himself as co-conspirator with Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Under tight shackles and brutal beating he could not endure the torture and was forced to write out a confession of treason, falsely admitting collusion with Xun.

sentences.zh: 獄具，左軍兵馬三百人領涯與王璠、羅立言，右軍兵馬三百人領賈餗、舒元輿、李孝本，先赴郊廟，徇兩市，乃腰斬於子城西南隅獨柳樹下。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, three hundred Left Army horses and troops led Ya, Wang Fan, and Luo Liyan; three hundred Right Army horses and troops led Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, and Li Xiaoben; first they were taken to the suburban altars, paraded through both markets, then beheaded at the waist beneath the Lone Willow south of the southwest corner of the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was closed, three hundred Left Army troops escorted Ya, Wang Fan, and Luo Liyan; three hundred Right Army troops escorted Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, and Li Xiaoben. They were first taken to the suburban altars and paraded through both markets, then beheaded at the waist beneath the Lone Willow southwest of the inner city.

sentences.zh: 涯以榷茶事，百姓怨恨詬罵之，投瓦礫以擊之。

translations.literal: Because of the tea monopoly affair, the common people resented and cursed Ya, throwing tiles and stones to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his tea monopoly policies, commoners cursed Ya in rage and pelted him with bricks and stones.

sentences.zh: 中書房吏焦寓、焦璇、臺吏李楚等十余人，吏卒爭取殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: More than ten men including Secretariat clerks Jiao Yu and Jiao Xuan and censorate clerk Li Chu—the clerks and soldiers competed to kill them, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten men, including Secretariat clerks Jiao Yu and Jiao Xuan and censorate clerk Li Chu, were killed in the scramble by the clerks and soldiers, and their estates were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 涯子工部郎中、集賢殿學士孟賢，太堂博士仲翔，其餘稚小妻女，連襟係頸，送入兩軍，無少長盡誅之。

translations.literal: Ya's son Meng Xian, director in the Ministry of Works and scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; the grand hall academician Zhongxiang; the rest—young wives and daughters—linked by the hem, bound at the neck, sent into the two armies; none young or old was spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's son Meng Xian, a director in the Ministry of Works and scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and the grand hall academician Zhongxiang, along with the younger wives and daughters, were bound at the neck and sent to the two armies—all were executed without exception, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 自涯已下十一家，資貨悉為軍卒所分。

translations.literal: From Ya downward, eleven households—all their goods were divided by the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The property of all eleven households from Ya's down was divided among the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 涯積家財鉅萬計，兩軍士卒及市人亂取之，竟日不盡。

translations.literal: Ya had amassed household wealth reckoned in the tens of thousands; soldiers of both armies and townspeople looted it wantonly—all day long it was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Ya had amassed a fortune beyond measure; soldiers of both armies and townspeople plundered it for a full day without carrying it all away.

sentences.zh: 涯博學好古，能為文，以辭藝登科。

translations.literal: Ya was broadly learned and fond of antiquity, able to compose prose, and entered the examination lists through literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was deeply learned and devoted to antiquity, a capable writer who had passed the examinations on literary merit.

sentences.zh: 踐揚清峻，而貪權固寵，不遠邪佞之流，以至赤族。

translations.literal: He trod a path clear and lofty, yet craved power and clung to favor, not keeping distant from wicked flatterers—thus reaching extermination of the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued a reputation for integrity, yet hoarded power and courted favor, consorting with corrupt sycophants until his entire clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 涯家書數萬卷，侔於秘府。

translations.literal: Ya's household books numbered tens of thousands of scrolls, matching the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's private library held tens of thousands of scrolls, rivaling the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 前代法書名畫，人所保惜者，以厚貨致之；

translations.literal: Calligraphy and famous paintings of former ages that men treasured, he obtained with heavy payment;
translations.idiomatic: For celebrated calligraphy and paintings of past ages that others cherished, he paid lavish prices;

sentences.zh: 不受貨者，即以官爵致之。

translations.literal: those who would not accept payment, he obtained with official rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: when money would not suffice, he secured them with official ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 厚為垣竅，而藏之復壁。

translations.literal: He built thick walls with hidden niches and stored them in hidden chambers behind walls.
translations.idiomatic: He built thick walls with secret compartments and hid them in concealed vaults.

sentences.zh: 至是，人破其垣取之，或剔取函奩金寶之飾與其玉軸而棄之。

translations.literal: At this time people broke his walls to take them; some stripped the gold and jewels from their caskets and the jade rollers and discarded the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At that point looters broke through his walls; some stripped the gold fittings and jade rollers from the cases and threw the works themselves away.

sentences.zh: 涯之死也，人以為冤。

translations.literal: At Ya's death, people regarded it as injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Ya was killed, many considered it a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使劉從諫三上章，求示涯等三相罪名，仇士良頗懷憂恐。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi military commissioner Liu Congjian submitted three memorials requesting disclosure of the crimes of Ya and the other three chancellors; Qiu Shiliang was greatly apprehensive and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, submitted three memorials demanding disclosure of the charges against Ya and the other three chancellors; Qiu Shiliang grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 初宦官縱毒，淩藉南司。

translations.literal: At first the eunuchs unleashed poison and trampled the southern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At first the eunuchs ran riot, brutalizing the civil officials.

sentences.zh: 及從諫奏論，兇焰稍息，人士賴之。

translations.literal: When Congjian memorialized and argued, the fierce flame slightly subsided; scholar-officials relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Congjian spoke out in memorials, the terror eased somewhat, and the scholar-official class owed him a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 時李逢吉為宰相，與璠親厚，故自郎官掌誥，便拜中丞。

translations.literal: At the time Li Fengji was chancellor and was close with Fan; therefore from draft edict officer he was at once invested as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji was then chancellor and on close terms with Fan, who was promoted straight from draft edict officer to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 恃逢吉之勢，稍橫。

translations.literal: Relying on Fengji's power, he grew somewhat overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by Fengji's influence, he grew increasingly arrogant.

sentences.zh: 嘗與左僕射李絳相遇於街，交車而不避。

translations.literal: Once he met Left Vice Director Li Jiang in the street and their carriages crossed without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Once he encountered Left Vice Director Li Jiang in the street and refused to give way when their carriages met.

sentences.zh: 絳上疏論之曰：「左、右僕射，師長庶僚，開元中名之丞相。

translations.literal: Jiang submitted a memorial arguing, saying: "The left and right vice directors are masters to the myriad officials; in the Kaiyuan era they were called chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang memorialized the throne: "The left and right vice directors stand above the officials as their superiors; in the Kaiyuan era they were known as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 其後雖去三事機務，猶總百司之權。

translations.literal: Afterward, though removed from the three chief affairs of state, they still held overall authority over the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later, even after they were removed from the three chief seats of power, they still held sway over all departments.

sentences.zh: 表狀之中，不署其姓。

translations.literal: In memorials and reports their surnames are not written.
translations.idiomatic: In official documents their surnames need not be written.

sentences.zh: 尚書已下，每月合衙。

translations.literal: From ministers downward, they assemble at court monthly.
translations.idiomatic: From ministers downward, all attend court together each month.

sentences.zh: 上日百僚列班，宰相居上，中丞御史列位於廷。

translations.literal: On the first day the hundred officials line up in ranks; the chancellor sits above, censors and investigators take places in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the month officials line up in formation, with the chancellor at the head and the censors arrayed in the hall.

sentences.zh: 禮儀之崇，中外特異。

translations.literal: The elevation of ritual and propriety is specially distinct within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Their ceremonial precedence is uniquely distinguished, both inside and outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 所以自武德、貞觀已來，聖君賢臣，布政除弊，不革此禮，謂為合宜。

translations.literal: Therefore from Wude and Zhenguan onward, sage rulers and worthy ministers, promulgating policy and removing abuses, did not alter this ritual, deeming it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wude and Zhenguan reigns onward, sage emperors and worthy ministers reformed policy and abolished abuses, yet never changed this ritual—they judged it proper.

sentences.zh: 茍有不安，尋亦合廢。

translations.literal: If there is anything improper, it should also in time be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: If anything about it were wrong, it ought likewise to be revised.

sentences.zh: 近年緣有才不當位，恩加特拜者，遂從權便，不用舊儀。

translations.literal: In recent years, because some talents were not in fitting posts but received special grace and extraordinary appointment, they then followed expedient power and did not use the old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, when men of talent were promoted out of turn by special favor, the old ceremonies were set aside for convenience.

sentences.zh: 酌於群情，事實未當。

translations.literal: Weighing it against the feelings of the masses, the matter is truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against general opinion, these practices are plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 今或有僕射初除，就中丞院門相看，即與欲參何殊。

translations.literal: Now when some newly appointed vice director goes straight to the censorate gate to pay a visit, how is that different from seeking an audience?
translations.idiomatic: When a newly appointed vice director goes at once to the censorate gate to call on the censor-in-chief, what difference is there from begging an audience?

sentences.zh: 或中丞新授，亦無見僕射處。

translations.literal: Or when a censor-in-chief is newly appointed, there is likewise no place to see the vice director.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor-in-chief is newly appointed, there is no proper occasion for him to call on the vice director either.

sentences.zh: 及參賀處，或僕射先至，中丞後來，憲度乖宜，尊卑倒置。

translations.literal: At places of congratulatory audience, sometimes the vice director arrives first and the censor-in-chief comes later—discipline and propriety are wrong, honor and inferior rank inverted.
translations.idiomatic: At congratulatory audiences, a vice director sometimes arrives before the censor-in-chief—protocol is violated and precedence reversed.

sentences.zh: 倘人才忝位，自合別授賢良；

translations.literal: If talent unworthily holds a post, naturally one should separately appoint the worthy;
translations.idiomatic: If a man is unfit for his rank, he should simply be given another appointment;

sentences.zh: 若朝命守官，豈得有虧法制？

translations.literal: if by court command one holds office, how could one be allowed to impair law and institutions?
translations.idiomatic: but once the court assigns a man to an office, how can he be allowed to undermine the regulations?

sentences.zh: 伏望下百僚詳定事體，使永可遵行。」

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully hopes the hundred officials below may examine and fix the substance of the matter, so that it may always be followed."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully ask that the officials be convened to settle these matters once and for all, so that proper practice may endure."

sentences.zh: 敕旨令兩省詳議。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript ordered the two departments to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict directed the two departments to consider the matter in detail.

sentences.zh: 兩省奏曰：「元和中，伊慎忝居師長之位，太常博士韋謙削去舊儀。

translations.literal: The two departments memorialized, saying: "In the Yuanhe era, Yi Shen unworthily occupied the position of master; Grand Music Master Academician Wei Qian cut away the old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The two departments replied: "In the Yuanhe era, when Yi Shen unworthily held the post of vice director, Grand Music Master Academician Wei Qian abolished the old ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今李絳所論，於禮甚當。」

translations.literal: What Li Jiang now argues is very fitting to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang's argument is entirely correct on ritual grounds."

sentences.zh: 逢吉素惡絳之直，天子雖許行舊儀，中書竟無處分，乃罷璠中丞，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Fengji had long hated Jiang's forthrightness; though the Son of Heaven permitted restoring the old ritual, the Secretariat in the end took no disposition; he then removed Fan as censor-in-chief and transferred him to vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji had long resented Jiang's bluntness. Though the Emperor approved restoring the old ceremonies, the Secretariat took no action; instead Fan was removed as censor-in-chief and made vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 尋罷絳僕射，以太子少師分司東都。

translations.literal: Soon Jiang was removed as vice director and made junior mentor to the heir apparent with duty at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was soon dismissed as vice director and sent to the eastern capital as junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其弄權怙寵如此。

translations.literal: Such was his manipulating power and relying on favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent of his abuse of power and court favor.

sentences.zh: 璠二年七月出為河南尹。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year Fan went out as Henan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 2 Fan was appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，以本官權知東都選。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, with his existing office he acted as supervisor of the eastern capital selection.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 2 (828) he served in his existing post as acting supervisor of civil service examinations at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，轉尚書右丞，敕選畢入朝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was transferred to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs; an edict ordered that when selection was complete he enter court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was transferred to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and ordered to return to court once the examinations were complete.

sentences.zh: 三年，改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to vice minister of civil office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made vice minister of civil office.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year he was invested as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 4 he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遷左丞，判太常卿事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to left vice director and adjudicated affairs of the grand master of court music.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was promoted to left vice director and given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，檢校禮部尚書、潤州刺史、浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year he was made acting minister of rites, prefect of Runzhou, and surveillance commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 6 he was appointed acting minister of rites, prefect of Runzhou, and surveillance commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 八年，李訓得幸，累薦於上。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Li Xun gained favor and repeatedly recommended Fan to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Li Xun won the Emperor's favor and repeatedly recommended Fan to the throne.

sentences.zh: 召還，復拜右丞。

translations.literal: He was recalled and again invested as right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was recalled and reappointed right vice director.

sentences.zh: 璠以逢吉故吏，自是傾心於訓，權幸傾朝。

translations.literal: Fan, as an old subordinate of Fengji, from then on poured his heart into Xun; power and favor tilted the court.
translations.idiomatic: As a former protégé of Fengji, Fan thereafter devoted himself to Xun and rose to unrivaled power at court.

sentences.zh: 九年五月，遷戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year he was transferred to minister of revenue and adjudicated the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 9 he was made minister of revenue with charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 謝日，召對浴堂，錫之錦彩。

translations.literal: On the day of thanksgiving for appointment he was summoned for audience in the Bath Hall and granted brocades.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he thanked the throne for his appointment, he was summoned to audience in the Bath Hall and rewarded with brocades.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，李訓將誅內官，令璠召募豪俠，乃授太原節度使，托以募爪牙為名。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, as Li Xun was about to kill the inner officials, he ordered Fan to recruit bold adventurers; Fan was then made military commissioner of Taiyuan, under the pretext of recruiting strong-arm men.
translations.idiomatic: That November, as Li Xun prepared to move against the eunuchs, he had Fan recruit men of violence and appoint him military commissioner of Taiyuan on the pretext of raising a private guard.

sentences.zh: 訓敗之日，璠歸長興裏第。

translations.literal: On the day Xun failed, Fan returned to his residence in Changxing Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun's plot collapsed, Fan fled to his home in Changxing Lane.

sentences.zh: 是夜為禁軍所捕，舉家下獄；

translations.literal: That night he was seized by the imperial guard; the whole household was thrown into prison;
translations.idiomatic: That night the palace guard seized him and his entire household was imprisoned;

sentences.zh: 斬璠於獨柳樹，家無少長皆死。

translations.literal: Fan was beheaded at the Lone Willow; in the household none young or old survived.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was beheaded at the Lone Willow, and every member of his family, young and old, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 璠子遐休，直弘文館。

translations.literal: Fan's son Xiaxiu served at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's son Xiaxiu was an attendant scholar at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 李訓舉事之日，遐休於館中禮上，同職駕部郎中令狐定等五六人送之，是日悉為亂兵所執。

translations.literal: On the day Li Xun launched the affair, Xiaxiu at the hall performed the rite toward the Emperor; five or six colleagues of the same office including Linghu Ding, director in the Transport Department, escorted him—all were seized by disorderly troops that day.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Li Xun acted, Xiaxiu was at the hall performing rites for the Emperor. Five or six colleagues, including Linghu Ding of the Transport Department, escorted him—and all were seized by the mutinous troops that day.

sentences.zh: 定以兄楚為僕射，軍士釋之，獨執遐休誅之。

translations.literal: Ding, because his elder brother Chu was vice director, was released by the soldiers; they alone seized Xiaxiu and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ding's elder brother Chu was a vice director, the soldiers released him but seized Xiaxiu alone and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 初璠在浙西，繕城壕。

translations.literal: At first when Fan was in Zhexi, he repaired the city moat.
translations.idiomatic: While Fan was in Zhexi he had the city moat repaired.

sentences.zh: 役人掘得方石，上有十二字，云：「山有石，石有玉，玉有瑕，瑕即休。」

translations.literal: Laborers digging obtained a square stone; on it were twelve characters, saying: "The mountain has stone; the stone has jade; the jade has a flaw; the flaw means extinction."
translations.idiomatic: Laborers digging up earth found a square stone inscribed with twelve characters: "The mountain has stone; the stone has jade; the jade has a flaw; the flaw means extinction."

sentences.zh: 璠視莫知其旨，京口老人講之曰：「此石非尚書之吉兆也。

translations.literal: Fan looked but did not know its meaning; an old man of Jingkou explained it, saying: "This stone is not an auspicious omen for the minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fan could make nothing of it, but an old man of Jingkou explained: "This stone foretells no good for the minister.

sentences.zh: 尚書祖名崟，崟生礎，是山有石也。

translations.literal: The minister's grandfather was named Yin; Yin begot Chu—this is "the mountain has stone."
translations.idiomatic: The minister's grandfather was named Yin; Yin fathered Chu—that is "the mountain has stone."

sentences.zh: 礎生尚書，是石有玉也。

translations.literal: Chu begot the minister—this is "the stone has jade."
translations.idiomatic: Chu fathered the minister—that is "the stone has jade."

sentences.zh: 尚書之子名遐休，休，絕也。

translations.literal: The minister's son is named Xiaxiu; xiu means extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The minister's son is named Xiaxiu—and xiu means "end."

sentences.zh: 此非吉征。」

translations.literal: This is not an auspicious sign."
translations.idiomatic: This is no good omen."

sentences.zh: 果赤族。

translations.literal: And indeed his entire clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: And in the end his whole clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 賈餗，字子美，河南人。

translations.literal: Jia Su, styled Zimei, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su, courtesy name Zimei, was from Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖渭。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was named Wei.

sentences.zh: 大父寧。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Ning.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was named Ning.

sentences.zh: 餗進士擢第，又登制策甲科，文史兼美，四遷至考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Su passed the jinshi examination and also placed in the top category of the decree examination; accomplished in both letters and history, he was promoted four times to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Su passed the jinshi examination and ranked in the top tier of the palace decree exam. Skilled in both prose and history, he rose through four promotions to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，策召賢良，選當時名士考策，餗與白居易俱為考策官，選文人以為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing reign, an edict summoned worthies and good men; eminent men of the time were chosen to grade the examination essays. Su and Bai Juyi both served as essay examiners and selected literati of public repute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era, an imperial summons sought worthy men, and leading scholars of the day were chosen to grade the policy essays. Su and Bai Juyi both served as examiners and selected candidates known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官知制誥，遷庫部郎中，充職。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing office he was made Drafting Officer for Proclamations, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and fulfilled his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Drafting Officer for Proclamations in his current post, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and carried out his duties.

sentences.zh: 四年，為張又新所構，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was framed by Zhang Youxin and sent out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhang Youxin engineered his downfall, and he was posted out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 太和初，入為太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign he entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe era he returned to court as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二年，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year, in his existing office he was made Drafting Officer for Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was again made Drafting Officer for Proclamations while retaining his current rank.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year he was provisionally placed in charge of the civil service examinations of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he was temporarily put in charge of the Ministry of Rites examinations.

sentences.zh: 五年，榜出後，正拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, after the examination results were posted, he was formally appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, once the results were announced, he was formally appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡典禮闈三歲，所選士七十五人，得其名人多至公卿者。

translations.literal: In all he presided over the examination hall for three years, selecting seventy-five candidates; many of those chosen rose to the ranks of duke and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years he ran the examinations and chose seventy-five candidates, many of whom later rose to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，遷京兆尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year he was moved to Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth year he became Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，檢校禮部尚書、潤州刺史、浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was made acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Runzhou, and Governor of Zhexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was appointed acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Runzhou, and Governor of Zhexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 制出未行，拜中書侍郎、同平章事，進金紫階，封姑臧男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Before the appointment edict could take effect, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor, advanced to the golden-purple rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Guzang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Before that appointment could take effect, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor, raised to the golden-purple rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Guzang, and granted a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加集賢殿學士，監修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and put in charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and placed in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，李訓事發，兵交殿廷，禁軍肆掠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year Li Xun's plot broke out; soldiers clashed in the palace hall and the imperial guard plundered at will.
translations.idiomatic: That November Li Xun's plot erupted. Troops fought in the palace hall, and the imperial guard looted freely.

sentences.zh: 餗易服步行出內，潛身人間。

translations.literal: Su changed clothes and walked out of the inner palace, hiding himself among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Su changed clothes, walked out of the palace on foot, and went into hiding among the people.

sentences.zh: 翌日，自投神策軍，與王涯等皆族誅。

translations.literal: The next day he turned himself in to the Shence Army; he and Wang Ya and the others were all executed to the extermination of their clans.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he surrendered to the Shence Army. He, Wang Ya, and the others were all executed along with their entire clans.

sentences.zh: 餗雖中立自持，然不能以身犯難，排斥奸纖，脂韋其間，遂至覆族。

translations.literal: Although Su maintained a stance of neutrality, he did not risk himself to meet the crisis, drive out the wicked and the sly, but drifted soft and complacent between the factions—and so brought ruin upon his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Su had kept to a neutral course, yet he would not risk himself in the crisis, drive out the wicked and the cunning, or stand firm between the factions. He drifted along in soft complacency, and so his clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 逢時多僻，死非其罪，世多冤之。

translations.literal: The times were unusually perilous; his death was not for his crimes, and many in the world considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The age was treacherous, and his death did not fit his crimes. Many regarded him as wronged.

sentences.zh: 舒元輿者，江州人。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanyu was a native of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanyu was a native of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元和八年登進士第，釋褐諸府從事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Yuanhe reign he passed the jinshi examination and, upon leaving office robes, served in various prefectural staff positions.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and, after taking up office, served on the staffs of various prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太和初，入朝為監察，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign he entered court as a Supervising Censor and was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe era he entered court as a Supervising Censor and was later made Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，天寶中，玄宗祀九宮壇，次郊壇行事，禦署祝板。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Tianbao reign, Emperor Xuanzong sacrificed at the Altar of the Nine Palaces; following the suburban altar rites he personally signed the prayer boards.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Tianbao era, Emperor Xuanzong sacrificed at the Altar of the Nine Palaces. After the suburban altar rites he personally signed the prayer boards.

sentences.zh: 元輿為監察，監祭事，以為太重，奏曰：「臣伏見祀九宮貴神祝板九片，陛下親署禦名，及稱臣於九宮之神。

translations.literal: Yuanyu was a Supervising Censor overseeing the sacrificial ceremonies; he considered the practice excessive and memorialized, saying: "Your subject has observed that for the sacrifice to the exalted spirits of the Nine Palaces there are nine prayer boards, upon which Your Majesty personally inscribes your imperial name and styles yourself as subject before the spirits of the Nine Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu, serving as Supervising Censor in charge of the sacrifices, thought the ceremony excessive and memorialized: "Your subject has seen that the sacrifice to the exalted spirits of the Nine Palaces requires nine prayer boards, on which Your Majesty personally writes your imperial name and calls yourself subject before the spirits of the Nine Palaces.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以天子之尊，除祭天地宗廟之外，無合稱臣者。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that in the dignity of the Son of Heaven, apart from sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, there is no appropriate occasion to style oneself subject.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject submits that in the majesty of the Son of Heaven, apart from sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, there is no proper occasion to call oneself subject.

sentences.zh: 王者父天母地，兄日姊月。

translations.literal: The king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother, the sun as elder brother and the moon as elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: The king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother, the sun as elder brother and the moon as elder sister.

sentences.zh: 而貴神以九宮為目，是宜分方而守其位。

translations.literal: Yet these exalted spirits take the Nine Palaces as their designation—they should each keep to their allotted quarter and guard their positions.
translations.idiomatic: These exalted spirits, however, are identified with the Nine Palaces and ought each to keep to their quarter and hold their proper place.

sentences.zh: 臣數其名號，太一、天一、招搖、軒轅、鹹池、青龍、太陰、天符、攝提也。

translations.literal: Your subject enumerates their names: Grand Unity, Celestial Unity, Swaying Brilliance, Yellow Thearch, Salt Pool, Azure Dragon, Grand Yin, Celestial Seal, and Swooping Handle.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject counts their names: Grand Unity, Celestial Unity, Swaying Brilliance, Yellow Thearch, Salt Pool, Azure Dragon, Grand Yin, Celestial Seal, and Swooping Handle.

sentences.zh: 此九神，於天地猶子男也，於日月猶侯伯也。

translations.literal: These nine spirits, with respect to Heaven and Earth, are like marquises and barons; with respect to the sun and moon, they are like feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: These nine spirits stand to Heaven and Earth as marquises and barons, and to the sun and moon as feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 陛下為天子，豈可反臣於天之子男耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the Son of Heaven—how can you in reverse style yourself subject before sons and barons of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven—how can you in turn call yourself subject before the sons and barons of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為過。

translations.literal: Your subject privately considers this a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes this is improper.

sentences.zh: 縱陰陽者流言其合祀，則陛下當合稱『皇帝遣某官致祭於九宮之神』，不宜稱臣與名。

translations.literal: Even should yin-yang practitioners circulate rumors favoring joint sacrifice, then Your Majesty should collectively style the formula "The Emperor sends a certain official to perform sacrifice to the spirits of the Nine Palaces"—it is not fitting to style oneself subject or to inscribe one's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Even if yin-yang practitioners spread talk of joint sacrifice, Your Majesty should use a formula such as "The Emperor sends a certain official to perform sacrifice to the spirits of the Nine Palaces." It is not fitting to call oneself subject or to inscribe one's personal name.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚瞽；

translations.literal: Though your subject is dull and blind;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject may be dull and blind,

sentences.zh: 未知其可。

translations.literal: I do not know whether this is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: but I do not know whether this proposal is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 乞下禮官詳議。」

translations.literal: I beg that the ritual officials be ordered to deliberate in detail."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the matter be referred to the ritual officials for detailed deliberation."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋轉刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元輿自負奇才，銳於進取，乃進所業文章，乞試效用，宰執謂其躁競。

translations.literal: Yuanyu, confident in his exceptional talent and keen to advance, submitted writings of his own composition and begged for a trial of his usefulness; the chief ministers considered him restless and overreaching.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu, confident in his own brilliance and eager to rise, submitted his writings and asked to be tested in office. The chief ministers judged him restless and overreaching.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，改授著作郎，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year he was reassigned as Editorial Director, serving in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year he was reassigned as Editorial Director with duty in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時李訓丁母憂在洛，與元輿性俱詭激，乘險蹈利，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xun was in mourning for his mother in Luoyang; he and Yuanyu were both of a nature inclined to eccentric audacity, seizing peril for profit, and they got on exceedingly well.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xun was mourning his mother in Luoyang. He and Yuanyu were both audacious and unorthodox by nature, ready to seize danger for profit, and they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 及訓為文宗寵遇，復召為尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Xun came into Emperor Wenzong's favor, Yuanyu was recalled as a Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun won Emperor Wenzong's favor, Yuanyu was recalled to court as a Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，以右司郎中知臺雜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as Right Director in the Secretariat and managed Bureau correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, as Right Director in the Secretariat, he was put in charge of Bureau correspondence.

sentences.zh: 七月，權知中丞事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was provisionally placed in charge of the affairs of the Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was temporarily placed in charge of the Censor-in-Chief's affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜御史中丞，兼判刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief, concurrently overseeing the Vice Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and concurrently placed in charge of the Vice Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 是月，以本官同平章事，與訓同知政事。

translations.literal: That month, in his existing office he was made Concurrent Grand Councilor and together with Xun shared in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was made Concurrent Grand Councilor in his current post and shared governance with Xun.

sentences.zh: 而深謀詭算，熒惑主聽，皆生於二兇也。

translations.literal: Yet their deep scheming and cunning stratagems, their bewildering of the sovereign's hearing—all arose from these two villains.
translations.idiomatic: Their deep plotting, cunning schemes, and bewildering of the emperor's judgment all sprang from these two villains.

sentences.zh: 訓竊發之日，兵自內出。

translations.literal: On the day Xun launched his plot, troops sallied from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xun launched his plot, troops burst out from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 元輿易服單馬出安化門，為追騎所擒，送左軍族誅之。

translations.literal: Yuanyu changed clothes and rode out alone through the Anhua Gate; pursuing horsemen seized him, and he was sent to the Left Army and executed to the extermination of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu changed clothes and rode alone out the Anhua Gate. Pursuing horsemen captured him, and he was handed over to the Left Army and executed along with his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 郭行余者，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: Guo Xingyu also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xingyu also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 太和初，累官至楚州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign he rose through repeated promotions to prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe era he rose through successive promotions to prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，移刺汝州，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to prefect of Ruzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to prefect of Ruzhou and made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 九月，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he entered the capital as Chief Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to court as Chief Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 李訓在東都時，與行余親善，行余數相餉遺，至是用為九列，十一月，訓欲竊發，令其募兵，乃授邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Xun was in the Eastern Capital he was on close terms with Xingyu; Xingyu frequently sent him gifts and provisions. At this time he was used for the Nine Ministers. In the eleventh month, when Xun intended to launch his plot, he ordered Xingyu to raise troops and then appointed him military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xun was in the Eastern Capital he was on friendly terms with Xingyu, and Xingyu often sent him gifts. By then he had risen to one of the Nine Ministers. In the eleventh month, as Xun prepared to launch his plot, he ordered Xingyu to raise troops and then appointed him military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 訓敗，族誅。

translations.literal: When Xun was defeated, his clan was executed to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was defeated, Xingyu's clan was executed to extinction.

sentences.zh: 羅立言者，父名歡。

translations.literal: Luo Liyan's father's name was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Liyan's father was named Huan.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，登進士第。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，檢校主客員外郎，為鹽鐵河陰院官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli reign he was made acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Receptions and served as an officer of the Heyin office of the Salt and Iron Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Baoli era he was acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Receptions and served as an officer of the Heyin office under the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 二年，坐糴米不實，計贓一萬九千貫，鹽鐵使惜其吏能，定罪止削所兼侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was punished for falsifying grain purchases; the embezzled sum was reckoned at nineteen thousand strings of cash. The Salt and Iron Commissioner, valuing his administrative ability, fixed the sentence only to stripping him of his concurrent post as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was convicted of falsifying government grain purchases, with embezzlement reckoned at nineteen thousand strings of cash. The Salt and Iron Commissioner, reluctant to lose his talent as an administrator, punished him only by stripping him of his concurrent post as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為司農少卿，主太倉出納物，以貨厚賂鄭註，李訓亦重之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe reign he was Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, in charge of disbursements from the Grand Granary; he used goods to lavish bribes on Zheng Zhu, and Li Xun also held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, overseeing disbursements from the Grand Granary. He used goods to bribe Zheng Zhu lavishly, and Li Xun also valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 訓將竊發，須兵集事，以京兆府多吏卒，用立言為京兆少尹，知府事。

translations.literal: When Xun was about to launch his plot he needed troops gathered for the affair; because the Metropolitan Prefecture of Jingzhao had many clerks and soldiers, Liyan was made Junior Administrator of Jingzhao and put in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Xun prepared to launch his plot he needed troops assembled for the task. Because the Metropolitan Prefecture of Jingzhao had many clerks and soldiers, Liyan was made Junior Administrator of Jingzhao and put in charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 訓敗日，族誅。

translations.literal: On the day Xun was defeated, his clan was executed to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xun was defeated, Liyan's clan was executed to extinction.

sentences.zh: 長安縣令孟琯貶硤州長史，萬年縣令姚中立朗州長史。

translations.literal: Meng Guan, magistrate of Chang'an County, was demoted to chief administrator of Xiazhou; Yao Zhongli, magistrate of Wannian County, was demoted to chief administrator of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guan, magistrate of Chang'an County, was demoted to chief administrator of Xiazhou, and Yao Zhongli, magistrate of Wannian County, was demoted to chief administrator of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 以兩縣捕賊官受立言指使故也。

translations.literal: This was because the arresting officers of both counties had acted at Liyan's direction.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the arresting officers of both counties had acted on Liyan's orders.

sentences.zh: 初立言集兩縣吏卒，萬年捕賊官鄭洪懼禍托疾，既而詐死，令家人喪服聚哭。

translations.literal: Earlier Liyan had assembled the clerks and soldiers of both counties; Zheng Hong, the arresting officer of Wannian, fearing disaster, pleaded illness, then feigned death and had his family don mourning garments and gather to wail.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liyan had assembled the clerks and soldiers of both counties. Zheng Hong, the arresting officer of Wannian, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and then faked his death, having his family put on mourning clothes and gather to wail.

sentences.zh: 姚中立陰知其故，恐以詐聞，不免其累，乃以狀告洪之詐。

translations.literal: Yao Zhongli secretly knew the reason; fearing that if the fraud were reported he would not escape involvement, he submitted a report of Hong's deception.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zhongli secretly knew what had happened. Fearing that if the fraud came to light he would not escape blame, he submitted a report exposing Hong's deception.

sentences.zh: 仇士良拘洪入軍，洪銜中立之告，謂士良曰：「追集所由，皆因縣令處分，予何罪也。」

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang seized Hong and brought him into the army; Hong bore a grudge over Zhongli's report and said to Shiliang: "Those summoned and assembled were all under the magistrate's orders—what crime is mine?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang seized Hong and brought him into the army. Resentful of Zhongli's report, Hong said to Shiliang: "Those who were summoned and assembled all acted on the magistrate's orders. What crime is mine?"

sentences.zh: 故中立坐貶，洪免死。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongli was demoted for his offense, and Hong was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: So Zhongli was demoted for his part, and Hong was spared death.

sentences.zh: 李孝本者，宗室之子也。

translations.literal: Li Xiaoben was a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoben was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 累官至刑部郎中，而依於訓、註以求進。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated promotions to Director in the Ministry of Justice, yet relied on Xun and Zhu to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Director in the Ministry of Justice, but relied on Xun and Zhu to advance his career.

sentences.zh: 舒元輿作相，訓用孝本知臺雜，權知中丞事，最預訓謀。

translations.literal: When Shu Yuanyu became chancellor, Xun used Xiaoben to manage Bureau correspondence and provisionally placed him in charge of the Censor-in-Chief's affairs; he was deepest in Xun's plotting.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu Yuanyu became chancellor, Xun put Xiaoben in charge of Bureau correspondence and temporarily placed him in charge of the Censor-in-Chief's affairs. He was deepest in Xun's plotting.

sentences.zh: 竊發之日，孝本從人殺內官十余人於殿廷。

translations.literal: On the day the plot was launched, Xiaoben followed others in killing more than ten inner officials in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the plot was launched, Xiaoben joined others in killing more than ten inner officials in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 知事不濟，單騎走投鄭註。

translations.literal: Realizing the affair would not succeed, he rode alone in flight to Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the affair would fail, he rode alone in flight toward Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 至咸陽西原，為追騎所捕，族誅之。

translations.literal: At the western plain of Xianyang he was captured by pursuing horsemen and executed to the extermination of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: At the western plain of Xianyang he was captured by pursuing horsemen and executed along with his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 坐訓、註而族者，凡十一家，人以為冤。

translations.literal: Those executed to clan extinction for their association with Xun and Zhu numbered eleven families in all; people considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven clans in all were executed for their ties to Xun and Zhu, and many regarded it as unjust.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王者之政以德，霸者之政以權。

translations.literal: The historiographer comments: The rule of a true king rests on virtue; the rule of a hegemon rests on power.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer comments: A true king governs through virtue; a hegemon governs through power.

sentences.zh: 古先後王，率由茲道，而遂能息人靖亂，垂統作則者。

translations.literal: The ancient kings before and after all followed this Way, and were thereby able to quiet the people, pacify disorder, and bequeath standards for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings, earlier and later, all followed this path and so were able to soothe the people, quell disorder, and leave standards for posterity.

sentences.zh: 如梓人共柯而殊工，良奕同枰而獨勝，蓋在得其術，則事無後艱。

translations.literal: Like woodworkers sharing the same axe-handle yet achieving different workmanship, or master players sharing the same board yet one alone prevailing—the key lies in obtaining the proper method, and then affairs need not face later hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Like woodworkers sharing the same handle yet producing different work, or master players at the same board yet only one prevailing—the difference lies in mastering the method, and then no task need later prove hard.

sentences.zh: 昭獻皇帝端冕深帷，憤其廝養，欲鏟宮居之弊，載澄刑政之源。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaoxian sat in dignified robes behind deep curtains, resentful of his palace attendants, wishing to uproot the evils of the inner quarters and purify the sources of law and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaoxian sat enthroned in formal robes behind deep curtains, resentful of the menials who served him, wishing to root out the evils of the inner palace and clarify the foundations of law and governance.

sentences.zh: 當宜禮一代正人，訪先朝耆德，修文教而厚風俗，設武備以服要荒。

translations.literal: He should have honored the upright men of his generation, sought out the venerable worthies of former reigns, cultivated literary teaching to deepen custom, and established military readiness to bring the frontier wastes to submission.
translations.idiomatic: He should have honored the upright men of his age, sought out the venerable worthies of earlier reigns, cultivated learning to strengthen custom, and built military readiness to bring the distant frontiers to heel.

sentences.zh: 俾西被東漸，皆陶於景化；

translations.literal: Then west and east alike would all be molded by his glorious transformation;
translations.idiomatic: Then east and west alike would have been shaped by his radiant transformation;

sentences.zh: 柔祗蒼昊，必降於闕祥，自然懷德以寧，無思不服。

translations.literal: the gentle earth and the azure heavens would surely send down auspicious signs upon the court—and naturally men would embrace virtue in peace, and none would think of refusing submission.
translations.idiomatic: Earth and Heaven would surely send down auspicious signs upon the court, and naturally the people would rest content in virtue, with none who would not submit.

sentences.zh: 況區區宦者，獨能悖化哉？

translations.literal: How could petty palace eunuchs alone overturn such transformation?
translations.idiomatic: How could petty palace eunuchs alone overturn such a transformation?

sentences.zh: 故豎刁、易牙，不廢齊桓之霸；

translations.literal: Thus Shu Dia and Yi Ya did not prevent Duke Huan of Qi's hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dia and Yi Ya did not prevent Duke Huan of Qi from achieving hegemony;

sentences.zh: 韓嫣、籍孺，何妨漢帝之明。

translations.literal: Han Yan and Ji Ru did not impair the brilliance of the Han emperor.
translations.idiomatic: nor did Han Yan and Ji Ru diminish the brilliance of the Han emperor.

sentences.zh: 蓋有管仲、亞夫之賢，屬之以大政故也。

translations.literal: It was because they had the worth of Guan Zhong and Zhou Yafu, to whom great affairs of state were entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: That was because they had men of the caliber of Guan Zhong and Zhou Yafu to whom the great affairs of state were entrusted.

sentences.zh: 此二君者，制禦閽寺，得其道也。

translations.literal: These two rulers controlled and restrained the gatekeepers of the palace—they grasped the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: These two rulers controlled the gatekeepers of the palace because they understood the proper way to do it.

sentences.zh: 而昭獻忽君人之大體，惑纖狡之庸儒。

translations.literal: Yet Zhaoxian suddenly neglected the great principles of rulership and was deluded by petty, cunning, mediocre Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxian, by contrast, suddenly neglected the great principles of kingship and was misled by petty, cunning mediocrities in scholar's garb.

sentences.zh: 雖終日橫經，連篇屬思，但得好文之譽，庸非致治之先。

translations.literal: Though he spent whole days poring over the classics and composing one linked essay after another, he won only a reputation for fine prose—not the prerequisites of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Though he spent whole days poring over the classics and composing essay after essay, he won only a reputation for fine writing—not the foundations of good government.

sentences.zh: 且李訓者，狙詐百端，陰險萬狀，背守澄而勸鴆，出鄭註以擅權。

translations.literal: And Li Xun was a man of a hundred devious schemes and ten thousand forms of secret malice: he turned on Shoucheng and urged poison upon him, and sent Zheng Zhu forth to usurp power.
translations.idiomatic: As for Li Xun, he was a man of endless cunning and countless hidden malices: he betrayed Wang Shoucheng even while urging poison upon him, and sent Zheng Zhu forth to seize power.

sentences.zh: 只如盡隕四星，兼權八校，小人方寸，即又難知。

translations.literal: Consider only how, as four stars fell in succession and eight command ranks were vested in a single man—the innermost thoughts of a petty man are then all the harder to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how, when four stars fell in succession and eight command ranks were combined in one man, the innermost thoughts of a petty man become all the harder to know.

sentences.zh: 但慮為蚤虱而采溪蓀，翻獲螾蜓之患也。

translations.literal: He only feared fleas and lice, yet in gathering river irises he instead brought upon himself the affliction of fireflies and dragonflies.
translations.idiomatic: He meant only to remove fleas and lice, yet in gathering river irises he brought upon himself a plague of gnats and dragonflies instead.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼明主！

translations.literal: Alas, enlightened sovereign!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, enlightened sovereign!

sentences.zh: 夫何不思，遽致血濺黃門，兵交青瑣。

translations.literal: Why did he not think? He rushed headlong to blood splashed at the Yellow Gate and soldiers clashing at the Blue Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Why did he not think? He rushed headlong into blood splashed at the Yellow Gate and soldiers clashing at the Blue Gate.

sentences.zh: 茍無籓後之勢，黃屋危哉！

translations.literal: Had there been no power of the frontier lords behind him, the imperial throne would have been imperiled!
translations.idiomatic: Had the frontier lords not stood behind him, the imperial throne would have been in peril!

sentences.zh: 涯、餗綽有士風，晚為利喪，致身鬼蜮之伍，何逃瞰室之災。

translations.literal: Ya and Su had the air of scholars, but in their later years they lost themselves to profit and cast their lot among demons and goblins—how could they escape the disaster of being watched from the rafters?
translations.idiomatic: Ya and Su had the air of scholars, but in their later years they lost themselves to profit and cast their lot among demons and goblins. How could they escape the disaster of being watched from the rafters?

sentences.zh: 非天不仁，子失道也！

translations.literal: It was not that Heaven was unkind—the sons had lost the Way!
translations.idiomatic: It was not that Heaven was unkind—the sons had lost the Way!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：奭、旦興周，斯、高亡秦。

translations.literal: The praise says: Shi and Dan raised Zhou; Si and Gao destroyed Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The praise says: Shi and Dan raised Zhou; Si and Gao destroyed Qin.

sentences.zh: 禍福非天，治亂由人。

translations.literal: Fortune and calamity are not from Heaven; order and chaos depend on men.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and calamity are not from Heaven; order and chaos depend on men.

sentences.zh: 訓、註奸偽，血頹象魏。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu were treacherous and false; blood toppled the elephant gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu were treacherous and false; blood toppled the elephant gate tower.

sentences.zh: 非時乏賢，君迷倒置。

translations.literal: It was not that the age lacked worthies—the ruler was deluded and set things upside down.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that the age lacked worthies—the ruler was deluded and set things upside down.
